channel.title: The Cross Section
channel.description: An AI-powered digest and trend analysis of hep-ex and hep-ph

item.title: Monday, October 19, 2026
item.description:
Two groups close the g⁶ pressure

Kajantie et al. arXiv:2610.23675 and Chala et al. arXiv:2610.23676 both report the complete 𝒪(g⁶⁾ pressure of hot Yang-Mills, a gap open for over two decades, and both land on the lattice side. Kajantie et al. get quantitative agreement with 4D lattice data over a broad temperature range. Chala et al. agree within errors with the older lattice-fitted coefficient. This follows last week’s N³LO cold-QED pressure (10-12), and the thermal loop-tree-duality method that did the work there reappears in the first paper. Unlike the other recent “next order” results, which mostly exposed the true error budget, these two are a direct pass of the dimensional-reduction EFT against data. Elsewhere, Crivellin et al. close off a |V_cb|-based escape from C_9, and NA61/SHINE reports an isospin effect it cannot explain.

Themes

Hot QCD pressure and N³LO building blocks

The two g⁶ papers, from different groups and presumably independent calculations, agree with each other and with the lattice. Devoto et al. arXiv:2610.22533 supply the three-loop rapidity beam-function kernels and so the full singular structure of color-singlet rapidity distributions at N³LO, which is the ingredient fully differential Higgs/DY work needs. Peng et al. arXiv:2610.22477 propose soft-hadron energy correlators as a flow probe, from p+p to Pb+Pb.

b→sℓℓ: the |V_cb| escape route closes

Crivellin et al. arXiv:2610.22490 test whether CKM unitarity violation, via NP contamination of |V_cb| and hence a smaller V_ts, can produce the lepton-flavor-universal b→sℓℓ deficit. They find a no-go: RG running breaks the custodial protection, and vector-like quarks fail EWPO and K/B_s mixing bounds. This bears on both the C_9 question and the inclusive/exclusive |V_cb| puzzle. LHCb’s first observation of Ξ_b⁻→Ξ⁻μ⁺μ⁻ arXiv:2610.22452 gives ℬ=(118±24±7±38)×10⁻⁸. The normalisation error is dominated by SU(3) breaking, the same symmetry that strained in the B→DP fit on 10-15.

Anomalies meeting their inputs, again

Abazajian et al. arXiv:2610.23713 find the 20 GeV halo excess depends strongly on foreground modelling, so it does not support a smooth NFW halo or a shared origin with the LZ event. That fits Cholis’s Fermi-bubble substructure argument from 10-09. No LZ model-building papers appeared today. Barčot et al. arXiv:2610.23474 review the neutrino anomalies and say recent results weakened several tensions without leaving an uncontested explanation, which matches last week’s gallium and IceCube-decoherence nulls. The NA61/SHINE result below is the day’s counter-current.

Exotics versus threshold dynamics

Garcia Tecocoatzi et al. arXiv:2610.22914 predict detectable 4P all-charm tetraquarks with J^PC=3^–,2^–. That sits against Swanson’s no-exotics di-J/ψ fit from 10-14. Damen et al. arXiv:2610.23240 give a sum-rule molecular reading of χ_c1(4010).

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.23675 Kajantie et al. — the nine nonfactorizing four-loop sum-integrals completing the hard contribution for general SU(N_c), and the explicit IR cancellation across scales. Read it for how the lattice comparison is made.
  • arXiv:2610.23676 Chala et al. — the same quantity from a separate calculation, and the first direct comparison with the lattice-fitted g⁶ coefficient. Read next to the paper above.
  • arXiv:2610.22490 Crivellin et al. — a clean statement of why a modified W-c-b vertex cannot fake C_9 without fine-tuning. A useful reference whenever someone proposes it.
  • arXiv:2610.23498 SHINE Collaboration — a charged-over-neutral kaon excess in central Ar+Sc at 8.8 and 11.9 GeV. They say it is not explained by known mechanisms, and they find a consistent excess from 2.6 to 200 GeV. Uncertainties are sizeable, so the question is whether other experiments confirm it.
  • arXiv:2610.23713 Abazajian et al. — a systematic foreground scan (281 diffuse configurations plus bubble templates) showing simulated mismodelling can produce NFW-like emission of the observed amplitude.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.23331 Reactor Antineutrino Detection with JUNO-TAO: Commissioning Performance and First Results — JUNO Collaboration (hep-ex). 2.8% energy resolution at the center, with first IBD excess over reactor-off data.
  • arXiv:2610.22418 Long-Lived Charge Trap Characterization for Rare-Event Searches with Skipper-CCDs — Ansh Desai et al. (physics.ins-det). 1787 traps characterized, with no significant effect on SENSEI’s single-electron rate. A hidden population is not excluded.
  • arXiv:2610.23332 Two-nucleon scattering amplitudes at light quark masses from lattice QCD — Jorge Baeza-Ballesteros et al. (hep-lat). Virtual states preferred in both isospin channels at M_π≈200 and 280 MeV.
  • arXiv:2610.23427 Effects of kinematic cuts on v_0(p_T) — Tribhuban Parida et al. (nucl-th). A low-p_T threshold biases v_0(p_T), and correcting it improves ALICE–ATLAS agreement.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.23675 — Complete g⁶ pressure of hot Yang–Mills theory (Keijo Kajantie et al.)

The missing nonlogarithmic hard coefficient is β̃_E1=6236±40. That converts to q_c(N_c=3,N_f=0)=-3591.2±16.9_pert±250_mag, consistent with the old lattice-inferred β̃_E1≃6000±600.

Method. - The 65 four-loop vacuum graphs give about 10⁵ sum-integrals. These reduce to 21 canonical structures, and ξ-dependence cancels at that stage. - Nine nonfactorizing sum-integrals were unknown. The authors evaluated them with thermal loop-tree duality. Matsubara sums are done analytically, and new local IR counterterms for zero-mode soft regions are added to BPHZ-style UV subtractions. The finite remainders were Monte Carlo integrated, at roughly 10⁶ CPU-hours. - The pole coefficients come out analytically. They confirm the previously inferred hard-scale IR poles and their explicit cancellation against EQCD/MQCD. - The method independently reproduces the known I_6.

Lattice comparison. The comparison uses Borsanyi et al. data in an EQCD-resummed scheme, with scale set by FAC and varied by a factor of 2. The band agrees with the data down to a few T_c. In the same scheme, g³ and g⁴ overshoot Stefan–Boltzmann and g⁵ undershoots. The authors read this as support for the “Laine conjecture”.

Caveats. - The magnetic constant B_G now dominates the error, by a factor of about 15 over the new perturbative piece. - The full result holds only for SU(3), because the four-loop MQCD matching is incomplete for general N_c. - The “only at g⁶” statement is tied to this resummation prescription. The authors note that other schemes behave better at lower orders.

arXiv:2610.23676 — The pressure of the gluon plasma at 𝒪(g_s⁶⁾, perturbatively (Mikael Chala et al.)

This is an independent route to the same quantity, giving q_c(0)=-3846±515. That is about 0.5σ from the value -3526(4)(55)(30) obtained by fitting the g⁶ formula to Borsanyi et al. trace-anomaly data over 10–1000 Λ_MS.

Method. - Background-field Feynman gauge, with a different propagator basis. - Reduction via SIRENA using unimodular loop-momentum changes and no genuine four-loop IBP. This yields 10 connected and 6 factorizable sum-integrals. - The connected integrals are evaluated numerically: Schwinger parameters, sector/subsector decomposition, partial Poisson resummation, and Sobol QMC with 4 Matsubara modes. - Poles are cross-checked by doing the hard-to-soft matching in the full bosonic SM 3D EFT. This needs a four-loop EFT vacuum counterterm that they compute for the first time. The resulting 22 equations have rank 14 and fix 7 pole combinations.

Lattice comparison. The strict expansion at μ̅=2πT matches the lattice within 3% above 2.5 Λ_MS, and within 1.5% from 3 to 1000 Λ_MS.

Caveats. - The error is about twice the Helsinki total. The two β_G errors alone account for only about ±170 of it, so the numerical sum-integral allowances dominate. - Both groups compare against the same lattice dataset, so the lattice check is not independent across the two papers. - The cross-check between the groups covers one shared master integral and the final q_c; the two central values differ by about 255.

arXiv:2610.22490 — Explaining b→sℓ⁺ℓ⁻ with CKM Unitarity Violation? A No-Go Theorem (Andreas Crivellin et al.)

Updated fit. The authors refit LFU b→sℓℓ data with new LHCb/CMS inputs. The best fit is C_9=-0.87, C_10=0.24, at 5.4σ (Δχ²≈33). This excludes the bins nearest the J/ψ.

The proposed escape. Rescaling V_cb, and hence V_ts, alone can buy about 23 units of χ². The natural operator for this is C⁽³⁾_23 (for C⁽³⁾_22, the required couplings are 𝒪(10)). But SMEFT/WET running gives C_9≈(33C⁽³⁾_23+24C⁽¹⁾_23) and C_10≈-20(30C⁽³⁾_23+27C⁽¹⁾_23), in units of TeV/Λ² at Λ=2 TeV. So custodial C⁽¹⁾⁼⁻C⁽³⁾ at the high scale does not survive.

Why it fails. - Requiring the right-sign δV_cb together with C_9<0 forces C_10≲-22C_9. - The only good-fit region is fine-tuned: C⁽¹⁾_23≈-1.1C⁽³⁾_23, C⁽³⁾_23≈-1. There the V_cb shift has the wrong sign and is overcompensated by Z-b-s. - A 10% positive shift already raises the B_s-mixing prediction by about 20%. - Vector-like quarks at 2 TeV, either U alone or the custodial pairs D+T_2 and T_1+T_2, cap C_9 below a quarter of the needed size, given B_s mixing, EWPO and ϵ_K.

Scope caveats. - Right-handed currents (O_Hud) are excluded. The authors argue these cannot resolve the inclusive/exclusive V_cb split. - The analysis fixes the scale at 2 TeV. - The underlying anomaly still rests on form-factor and nonlocal-hadronic inputs.

item.title: Friday, October 16, 2026
item.description:
A threshold excess, fitted with the PDFs

Ball et al. arXiv:2610.21479 take the tt̅ threshold excess, the thing CMS’s toponium result made a headline, and ask what it looks like in a global PDF analysis. They fit ATLAS and CMS differential data with correlated PDF, m_t and α_s uncertainties. They find nothing at 8 TeV and just over 2σ at 13 TeV. They also find a strong Δ–m_t correlation. That is a much quieter reading than CMS’s 6.1σ, from a different handle on the same region. Elsewhere, LZ gets one paper that moves the argument from the solar bound to the halo, and two precision inputs (lattice HVP, solar gallium) land on the SM side.

Themes

Threshold, toponium, and the inputs they depend on

Ball’s result is a reminder that any tt̅-threshold claim has to be quoted jointly with m_t. It also bears on the toponium-vs-CP-odd-scalar question. Around it sit precision-QCD building blocks. Gehrmann et al. arXiv:2610.20820 deliver all three-loop four-point masters with one off-shell leg, including a 371-integral family, which is the missing piece for N³LO V/H+jet. Seymour arXiv:2610.22102 damps spurious singularities in dipole subtraction. Alsairafi arXiv:2610.21813 compares decay modelling in tt̅ tt̅.

LZ: now the halo tail is on trial

Graham et al. arXiv:2610.21041 show how the thermal Higgsino could survive the solar-neutrino bound, the constraint most 248 keV models have been designed around. It needs a different high-velocity dark-matter tail from the LMC-motivated simulations. That shifts the argument from model-building to halo simulations, which echoes the halo-marginalization point from 10-06. The paper also proposes heavy-element paleodetectors and large neutrino detectors as tests that do not depend on xenon.

Anomalies meeting their inputs

  • Elliott et al. arXiv:2610.22219 use the Sun as a calibrated source and find no gallium anomaly: SAGE+GALLEX/GNO at 66.1±3.1 SNU against 67.5⁺¹.4_-1.1 expected.
  • Alexandrou et al. arXiv:2610.22224 (ETMC) get a_μ^HVP=(714.9±8.1)×10⁻¹⁰ at about 1%, agreeing with other lattice groups and widening the gap to pre-CMD3 data-driven values.
  • Li et al. arXiv:2610.20945 get a QCD sum-rule a_τ^HVP of (3.501±0.048)×10⁻⁶, and their combined a_μ^HVP sits on the lattice side too.

Hadronization and tooling

Janik et al. arXiv:2610.20793 use tensor-network string breaking to motivate the Lund area law. Bonanno et al. arXiv:2610.20747 mitigate topological freezing at 0.03 fm with stochastic normalizing flows. That is the first lattice-side fix for the sampling problem under the strong-CP lattice program. Bierlich arXiv:2610.21897 shows Lorentz boosts silently lose precision in single-precision records and air-shower codes, though not in ordinary double-precision collider work.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.21479: The threshold excess with PDF, m_t and α_s correlations propagated. The Δ–m_t correlation is the number to check before quoting any significance.
  • arXiv:2610.21041: The first paper to say concretely what halo tail would rescue the thermal Higgsino. It also gives non-xenon discriminators between inelastic DM and other readings.
  • arXiv:2610.22219: Removes the gallium anomaly as a sterile-neutrino argument by using solar sources. It reads as a cross-section-independent check.
  • arXiv:2610.22224: Four lattice spacings down to 0.049 fm and boxes up to 7.7 fm, retuned to both FLAG and WP25 isospin-symmetric definitions.
  • arXiv:2610.20793: One collective mode carries over 99% of the string-breaking dynamics, and its decay follows a Gaussian survival law. Interesting for anyone who treats Lund as pure phenomenology.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.20751 Auditing anapole dark matter: the limits of model independence in dark matter effective field theory — Duncan K. Adams et al. (hep-ph). Different UV completions of the anapole operator give qualitatively different collider, relic and direct-detection signals, so “model-independent” EFT bounds do not always apply.
  • arXiv:2610.21982 First Observation of the Radiative Decay D⁰ →γω — BESIII Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). Seen at 6.0σ using a Particle Transformer, with ℬ=(2.12±0.40±0.25)×10⁻⁵.
  • arXiv:2610.20977 Disentangling geometry & growth in cosmic neutrino mass constraints — Fei Ge et al. (astro-ph.CO). Splitting ∑m_ν into geometry and growth parts shows both prefer “negative” masses at similar levels, passing the ΛCDM null test at 0.4σ.
  • arXiv:2610.22102 Spurious Singularities in Dipole Subtraction Cross Sections… — Michael H. Seymour (hep-ph). Dedicated to the memory of Stefano Catani, with whom the work was started.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.21479 — Determining the Threshold Excess in Top-Quark Pair Production through a Global PDF Analysis (Richard D. Ball et al.)

The fit. Ball and ter Hoeve float a threshold excess Δ alongside m_t, α_s(m_Z) and the PDFs. They use the Theory Covariance Method on ATLAS and CMS m_tt̅-differential data, measured against fixed-order NNLO QCD with NLO EW and missing-higher-order uncertainties. The Δ prior is deliberately broad, at 200% of a 6.43 pb (13 TeV) / 2.19 pb (8 TeV) central value.

Results. - 13 TeV: Δ= 14.14⁺⁶.44_-6.31 pb and m_t = 172.85⁺⁰.59_-0.58 GeV, which is 2.2σ from the continuum. The m_t error is 2.3× larger than in their Δ-free fit, and the correlation is ρ(Δ,m_t)=0.84. - 8 TeV: Δ= 0.57±3.83 pb, or 3.28⁺².66_-2.32 pb with positivity imposed, with ρ=0.69. They attribute the energy dependence to the gluon being probed at higher x at 8 TeV. - Conditioned on m_t=172.5 GeV: Δ= 11.14⁺⁴.08_-4.41 pb. This is close to the ATLAS (9.3 pb) and CMS (8.8 pb) toponium cross sections but with larger errors, which the authors suggest come from the PDF correlation.

Why it matters. Any threshold-excess number is effectively a statement about m_t as well. Conversely, m_t fits that ignore Δ absorb part of the excess.

Caveats. - No individual 13 TeV dataset deviates significantly except CMS dilepton, at about 2σ. The excess only appears in the combination, whose central value exceeds every individual one; the authors explain this as a BLUE-type correlated-combination effect. - The 68% intervals use only replicas with Δ > 0. - Bin migrations from the top width are neglected. - The ATLAS 13 TeV inputs use 36 fb⁻¹. - Δ is defined relative to fixed-order NNLO, not NRQCD.

The proposed way to break the Δ–m_t degeneracy is to add spin-correlation observables to the fit.

arXiv:2610.21041 — Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments (Peter W. Graham et al.)

The halo question. For the 1.1 TeV thermal Higgsino, the 248 keV event’s preferred splitting depends on the halo model, but stays below the solar-capture bound (δ ≲ 566 keV) in the standard ones:

Halo model Efficiency window Preferred δ (keV) Status
SHM LZ ROI (0–250 keV) 340–360 Excluded by solar bound
Simulated LMC LZ ROI 495–515 Excluded by solar bound
SHM / LMC Full 0–650 keV Contours drop below the Higgsino line Disfavoured
LMC tail cut 100× (w=0.0026%) Full 440–510 Moves up to the Higgsino line, still excluded
LMC tail extended to v_max=1100 km/s at 10% flux Full 500–600 Partly survives

Two numbers frame the last two rows: - The 100× flux reduction corresponds to w=0.0026%, two orders of magnitude below the usual benchmarks. - The 10% flux of the extended tail sits an order of magnitude below the lowest flux current simulations resolve.

The authors’ conclusion is that the Higgsino question becomes a halo-simulation-resolution question.

Proposed tests. - Pb paleodetectors (Laurionite, 60 cm³, 15 nm SAXs): cover most of the event contour. - Two different elements: fix m_χ and δ through the apex recoil energy. - Mineral-age scans: the signal-to-noise should peak at 50–100 Myr if the tail comes from the LMC. - JUNO with a (20 m)³ Pb or ²³⁸U shell: covers the 566–600 keV window, and measures δ directly from the photon line. Varying the shell yields the decay length, which is calculable for the Higgsino.

Caveats. - The analysis rests on a single event. - The contours are relative likelihoods, not goodness of fit. - The efficiency is assumed to stay near 1 up to 650 keV, beyond LZ’s conservative ROI. - The extended tail is admittedly speculative.

arXiv:2610.22219 — Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos (Steven R. Elliott et al.)

The calibration. Elliott and Robertson use the Sun as a calibrated source. Its strength is fixed by Borexino elastic-scattering fluxes (⁷Be, CNO), the SNO neutral-current ⁸B flux, and a luminosity-constrained pp flux of 5.966(27)×10¹⁰ cm⁻²s⁻¹. Survival probabilities use JUNO and Daya Bay mixing, and solar models enter only through the MSW density profile.

Result. The predicted rate is 67.5⁺¹.4_-1.1 SNU against a measured 66.1±3.1 SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO, a ratio of 0.980⁺⁰.050_-0.049. The radioactive-source experiments give 0.817⁺⁰.028_-0.048. More than 90% of the solar rate comes from the ground-state cross section derived via detailed balance.

Why it matters. This disfavours the proposed ~20% factorization breakdown (Cadeddu et al.), which sits roughly 3.5σ from the solar ratio, and any error in the ⁷¹Ga cross section more generally. It also validates the extraction and counting efficiencies of SAGE, Gallex and BEST.

Correction to the digest’s framing. This removes the mundane explanations, not the anomaly. The authors conclude that its “source evidently lies elsewhere” and say nothing against sterile neutrinos.

Caveat. The solar rate is dominated by pp neutrinos (40 of 67.5 SNU). The test therefore weights the cross section differently from the source experiments.

Full text was not supplied for arXiv:2610.22224 or arXiv:2610.20793, so they are not covered here.

Citation radar

A single paper, but a clear signal: attention is concentrated on LZ’s 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which has a 3.4σ local and 2.6σ global significance. The live question has shifted from whether endothermic dark matter can fit the event to which particle realizations survive complementary probes. Solar capture plus IceCube has become the main filter.

arXiv:2609.06760 — Solar Capture Tests of Inelastic Dark Matter after the LZ High-Recoil Event (Mattia Di Mauro et al.)

Di Mauro and Shaikh propagate three LZ-fitting interpretations through Solar capture, post-capture orbital evolution, and IceCube annihilation limits.

  • Thermal Higgsino. The authors independently confirm the Pospelov–Ramani exclusion, matching the thermalized endpoint to within 1–2 keV. IceCube requires δ ≳ 0.51–0.56 MeV, while the LZ-preferred splitting is about 377 keV. The gap survives the uncertainty in the loop-induced elastic cooling cross sections and a deliberately pessimistic WW/ZZ treatment.
  • Pseudo-Dirac vector model. The model captures plenty of dark matter, C⊙ = 1.53×10²⁰ s⁻¹, roughly at the naive equilibrium scale for the IceCube b-bbar limit. However, annihilation requires one χ₁ and one χ₂, and this two-state kinetics caps Γ_A at about 4.4×10¹⁴ s⁻¹, roughly 1.7×10⁵ below the limit.
  • Neutron-philic 𝒪₄ model. Capture is starved because it can proceed only on trace odd-neutron isotopes, leaving the equilibrium rate a factor of about 154 below the limit.

The paper flags real caveats: b-bbar is used only as a proxy for the annihilation spectrum, and re-excitation cycles need a full phase-space treatment.

With ~52 citations since its September posting, the likely draw is its function as a scorecard. It closes off the most predictive interpretation while stating plainly that endothermic explanations are not generically excluded. That gives both skeptics and model-builders something to cite. The paper itself references seven recent Solar-capture analyses of the event, pointing to a crowded, fast-moving subliterature. The citing papers themselves aren’t visible from the text, so this reading is inferred.

item.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026
item.description:
B→DP wants 60% SU(3) breaking

Bhattacharya et al. arXiv:2610.20611 refit B̅→DP together with B̅→D̅P, adding the direct and indirect CP asymmetries that appear when D⁰ and D̅⁰ interfere. The disagreement with the SU(3)_F-limit SM stays above 5σ. The SU(3)_F breaking needed to absorb it grows from ~20% with branching ratios alone to ~60% with all observables. At that size, “breaking” stops being a small correction to the flavor-symmetry expansion. The result sits beside August’s B→PP SU(3)_F puzzle, now on the charm side. Elsewhere, |V_cb| gets a proposal that avoids B decays entirely. LZ drops to one paper after yesterday’s five.

Themes

Flavor symmetry and |V_cb|

Bhattacharya et al. supply the tension. Marzocca arXiv:2610.18961 proposes measuring |V_cb| through b-tagged charged-current DIS, e⁻c→ν_e b. He projects ~0.8% at LHeC and 0.7% at FCC-eh, with systematics unrelated to the inclusive/exclusive fight in semileptonic decays. The EIC reaches only 20–30%. De Fazio et al. arXiv:2610.19917 summarize the Frascati semileptonic workshop on CKM status, form factors and LFU, which is a useful reference while R(D⁽*)) and |V_cb| both remain open.

Quantum information in scattering

Chu et al. arXiv:2610.18955 note that stabilizer Rényi entropy depends on an unspecified phase frame for helicity states. They define a rephasing-invariant version, and tree-level gluon scattering saturates its two- and three-channel ceilings. This gives the season’s “magic” thread a convention-independent definition. Ji et al. arXiv:2610.19711 treat soft-photon decoherence of a pion-pair density matrix as a flow in detector resolution. They tie the Lindblad jump operator to the soft Wilson line and recover real–virtual cancellation at the density-matrix level.

Hadron-structure inputs

Yang et al. arXiv:2610.19415 respond to the Fantômas claim of underestimated small-x pion PDF uncertainties. With an extended H1+ZEUS leading-neutron dataset, they strongly disfavor a vanishing pion gluon. Alexandrou et al. arXiv:2610.20362 add Nσ interpolators to suppress excited states in σ_πN. Since σ_πN was the hadronic input Bao et al. hedged with FLAG-vs-Roy–Steiner last week, the eventual number matters.

Dark-matter detectors, other jobs

Amaral et al. arXiv:2610.18971 use solar-neutrino data from LZ, XENONnT and PandaX-4T. They report that these data already constrain part of the complex-NSI explanation of the NOvA–T2K tension. COSINE-100 (Kim et al. arXiv:2610.19668) pushes NaI to a 0.49 keV threshold with an MLP noise filter. Deka arXiv:2610.18974 is the day’s only LZ paper: a 45 GeV exothermic freeze-in model, worked through several non-instantaneous reheating histories.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.20611: A >5σ SU(3)_F failure that grows to ~60% breaking once CP observables enter. Either the amplitude parametrization or the symmetry expansion needs rethinking.
  • arXiv:2610.18961: A high-energy |V_cb| at sub-percent precision with orthogonal systematics. Flavor-tag calibration is the stated bottleneck.
  • arXiv:2610.18971: The xenon experiments’ neutrino floor turned into a test of the NOvA–T2K tension. The authors say it probes NSI regions DUNE cannot.
  • arXiv:2610.19066: Zhang et al.’s Born–Oppenheimer χEFT reads the 10.513 GeV 1⁺⁺ as a mostly molecular X_b. It predicts a compact partner ~60 MeV below BB̅^*, which is a concrete search target.
  • arXiv:2610.20449: Castorina et al. impose strangeness conservation at the quark level, not the hadron level, which fixes the unsuppressed-ϕ problem in small systems at ~5σ. The same mechanism predicts how ΛΛ̅ spin correlations dilute with multiplicity.

From the community

  • arXiv:2610.19111 Pythia-Contrib: a modular contribution framework for the Pythia 8 event generator — Benoit Assi et al. (hep-ph). Pythia now has a route for third-party code that adds no dependencies to the core.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.20551 Top-Quark Mass Scheme Uncertainties in Higgs Boson Pair Production via Gluon Fusion — Clara Del Pio et al. (hep-ph). A threshold-aware MSR/MS prescription gives ⁺⁵.2%_-0.2%, a lopsided band for the self-coupling program.
  • arXiv:2610.19024 Two-loop gg→AA amplitudes near threshold and the double parton scattering singularity — Arunima Bhattacharya (hep-ph). The near-threshold angular logarithm is identified as the DPS singularity.
  • arXiv:2610.20132 A low-cost compact muon detector for millikelvin operation — Tengiz Ibrayev et al. (physics.ins-det). Below ~8 K each muon gives a double pulse, traced to a superconducting layer in the SiPM. The mechanism of the second pulse is not understood.
  • arXiv:2610.20507 Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter? — Samuel Gómez Gómez et al. (astro-ph.HE). The abstract opens with “No,” and the bounds support it.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.20611 — A global analysis of B̅→DP and B̅→D̅P decays (Bhubanjyoti Bhattacharya et al.)

Adding D⁰–D̅⁰ interference observables pushes the SU(3)_F-breaking requirement from ~20% to ~60%. The SU(3)_F-limit fit to all 25 observables (15 branching ratios, 6 direct and 4 time-dependent CP asymmetries, with β, β_s, γ fixed to world averages) gives χ²_min/dof=153.4/12. The branching ratios alone are already bad: B̅→DP gives 105/5. Splitting by strangeness, the ΔS=0 fit is excellent (0.2/1), but |T_1/T_0|-1=0.15±0.03 and |C_1/C_0|-1=0.36±0.13.

Allowing first-order breaking diagrams but capping their ratios at 30% leaves χ²_min=17.0, and every ratio saturates the cap. The dominant pulls come from 𝒜_CP(B⁻→D_CPπ⁻⁾ (χ²⁼¹⁰.3) and S(B̅⁰→D⁻π⁺⁾. Raising the cap to 60% brings χ²_min down to 2.8. The remainder is irreducible: - ~1.0 from an isospin-related pair of branching ratios; - ~1.4 from the measured S(D^±π^∓) central values exceeding the bound 2κ/(1+κ²⁾⁼⁰.0341 that their own branching ratios imply.

Alongside the ~1000% needed in B→PP, this is a second system where the symmetry expansion is under strain.

Caveats: - The 30% and 60% fits use 35 parameters for 25 observables, so there are no degrees of freedom. The case for >30% breaking rests on cap saturation and the χ²-vs-R scan. - Many fitted ratios are poorly determined (e.g. r_T_1=0.6±0.5). - The B̅→D̅P sector has only five measured branching ratios. - Isospin breaking is ignored.

arXiv:2610.18961 — Measuring V_cb at electron-proton colliders (David Marzocca)

The projection is a sub-percent |V_cb| from b-tagged charged-current DIS. The fit uses binwise ratios of b-tagged to flavour-inclusive CC counts in (x,y). It profiles projected PDFs, the other CKM elements, top background and tag calibration, with no |V_cb| prior or unitarity input. Projected precision:

Collider Luminosity Unpolarised Polarised
LHeC 1 ab⁻¹ 0.89% 0.79% (P_e=-0.8)
FCC-eh 2 ab⁻¹ — 0.67%
EIC — — 22–32%

At the EIC, |V_cb|=0 remains allowed within 3σ. For comparison, the PDG gives |V_cb|_excl=39.5±0.5 and |V_cb|_incl=42.0±0.5 (×10⁻³), so the LHeC number would be competitive with orthogonal systematics.

Calibration, not statistics, sets the floor. At the LHeC the error grows from 0.27% (statistics only) to 0.49% with CKM, PDF and top uncertainties, then to 0.79% once tag calibration is added. The b-efficiency calibration enters as roughly δ_b/2; its correlation with μ_cb is −64%. Halving calibration widths gives 0.60%, and a better tagger on top gives 0.55% at the LHeC and 0.40% at FCC-eh. Using today’s PDF4LHC21 instead of projected PDFs degrades the LHeC result to 1.0%. Mistag-shape uncertainties of 5% and 10% give 0.91% and 1.0%.

Caveats: - The calculation is Born-level with flat tag responses. - Radiative b production and photoproduction are not treated. - The neutral-current background is only modelled via an assumed electron-loss probability.

arXiv:2610.18971 — Direct Detection of Solar Neutrinos to Probe Tensions and Break Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Experiments (Dorian W. P. Amaral et al.)

For nucleon-only NSI, current LZ and XENONnT ⁸B CEνNS data already exclude part of the complex-ℰ_eτ region that resolves the NOvA–T2K tension (|ℰ|∼0.2, ϕ∼3π/2). They do not yet reach the ℰ_eμ region.

A 200 t·yr xenon detector (XLZD or PandaX-xT) with a 1 keV_nr threshold and 6% ⁸B flux uncertainty would nearly cover the ℰ_eτ 1σ region. For electron-only couplings, LZ’s ER data are not yet sensitive.

The degeneracy argument is structural. Oscillations see only differences of diagonal couplings, while scattering sees absolute couplings. Even after profiling over ℰ_μμ, current NR (and, for electron-only couplings, LZ ER) limits cut into DUNE’s degenerate (|ℰ_eτ|,ℰ_ee-ℰ_μμ) region. They do not reach the ℰ_ττ-ℰ_μμ region.

Caveats: - Results depend strongly on the assumed (η,φ) coupling configuration. - The NR analyses assume no background, with the 12% ⁸B flux uncertainty dominant. - XENONnT ER data are excluded because its pp flux, (10.2±2.0)×10¹⁰ cm⁻²s⁻¹, sits 2.6σ from Borexino. The NSI region it prefers is largely excluded by LZ.

Full texts for arXiv:2610.19066 and arXiv:2610.20449 were not supplied, so no deep dive is given for those picks.

item.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026
item.description:
IceCube closes Planck-suppressed decoherence

IceCube’s decoherence search arXiv:2610.14144 is the day’s cleanest result. It uses 368k atmospheric neutrinos at 0.5–100 TeV, an order of magnitude higher in energy than earlier searches, and finds nothing. It excludes natural Planck-suppressed decoherence for every Eⁿ scaling with 0≤n≤3, the first Planck-scale exclusion at n=3. Separately, LZ model-building rose to five papers, after last week’s one or two a day. Flavor proceedings say the R(D⁽*)) world-average tension is still there despite last month’s Belle II easing.

Themes

LZ: the Sun as a test, not a veto

Di Mauro arXiv:2610.14188 fits the event with a gauged U(1)_B mediator, m_χ≃0.19–4.5 TeV. He proposes a dedicated IceCube four-quark solar-capture analysis as one of the tests, which continues last week’s move from evading the solar bound to designing around it. Wang et al. arXiv:2610.16156 go after TeV Higgsinos through gluinos, with Run 2 exclusions near 2.2 TeV. Cerdeño et al. arXiv:2610.14178 note that compressed inert doublets predict the small splitting. Ahmed et al. arXiv:2610.15557 and Sahoo et al. arXiv:2610.18234 do not mention solar capture in their abstracts, so the holdouts are still with us.

b→c and b→s

  • Hu et al. arXiv:2610.17289 give parameter-free continuum-Schwinger form factors with R(D^*)=0.267(5), 2.8σ from experiment.
  • Warburton’s Belle/Belle II summary arXiv:2610.16617 finds the new results individually SM-consistent but the world averages still in tension. The September “easing” did not close the question.
  • LHCb arXiv:2610.14156 measures B⁰→K⁺π⁻μμ at high m_Kπ differentially for the first time. This is new input for the C_9 fights.

Thresholds instead of exotics

Swanson arXiv:2610.15248 fits the LHC di-J/ψ spectrum with a compact source rescattering through ten charmonium-pair channels, getting χ²/ndf = 56/50 with no exotic hadrons. That cuts against last week’s bound ccc̅c̅ claim and its 2⁺ link to the CMS structure. Colangelo arXiv:2610.14170 solves the Roy equations at variable pion mass and matches lattice data at 239 MeV, which sets up dispersive σ/ρ analyses of lattice spectra.

Tools leave the demo stage

Heimel et al.’s MadNIS arXiv:2610.17177 becomes MadGraph’s LO default, with speed-ups up to 250×. Menzo et al.’s HEPTABench arXiv:2610.18454 extends last month’s HEPToolBench into controlled agent evaluation. Adding domain tools lifts Haiku 4.5 from 8% to 79% on symbolic decays. Ma et al.’s SIDERIUS arXiv:2610.14024 scores agents on whether the models they produce are scientifically valid, not on raw score.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.14144: A clean null that removes a whole class of quantum-gravity phenomenology at its natural scale.
  • arXiv:2610.17177: Neural importance sampling is becoming the default most people will run without noticing. Check the amortization numbers.
  • arXiv:2610.15248: The no-exotics null hypothesis for di-J/ψ, with only three free background parameters. Every tetraquark paper should now have to beat it.
  • arXiv:2610.17213: Holguin defines what a generator should compute from detector operators. The one-loop result is directly sensitive to the recoil scheme, which makes it a principled yardstick for shower accuracy.
  • arXiv:2610.14188: The most complete single-model LZ paper so far, with dijet, relic and solar tests all specified.

From the community

  • arXiv:2610.14059 The Future of AI-assisted Physics: Discovering, Verifying and Organizing Results via Formalization — Sven Krippendorf et al. (hep-ph). A position paper on trust, credit, and why a checked proof does not certify that the definitions capture the physics.
  • arXiv:2610.14303 AI Acceleration of Muon Collider R&D — J. Scott Berg et al. (physics.acc-ph). A workshop report mapping AI use cases onto the muon collider’s bottlenecks.
  • arXiv:2610.16708 About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich… — Paul H Frampton (hep-th). A short tribute with recollections of Moscow visits in 1989–91.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.16496 Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO–supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt — Stéphane Fay et al. (astro-ph.CO). A distance-duality tilt removes more of the CPL preference than curvature does.
  • arXiv:2610.14806 Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe — Jintao Zou et al. (astro-ph.CO). GW amplitudes come out about 10× below Minkowski simulations, which matters for last week’s phase-transition cluster.
  • arXiv:2610.15493 Probing the chromo-electric dipole moment of top quark near the toponium production threshold at LHC — Kai Ma et al. (hep-ph). Toponium reframed as a CP probe.
  • arXiv:2610.16647 Experimental Demonstration of Soft-Tissue Muon Scattering Tomography — Dipanwita Banerjee et al. (hep-ex). Percent-level agreement with simulation on a thorax phantom.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.14144 — Planck-Scale Constraints on Quantum Gravity-Induced Neutrino Decoherence with IceCube (R. Abbasi et al.)

IceCube sees no oscillation damping in 368,071 up-going ν_μ events (10.7 yr, E_reco 0.5–100 TeV). The sample is the same as the sterile-neutrino analysis, now at 99.9% purity and split into starting and throughgoing tracks. The decoherence fits use a Lindblad operator with a single rate Γ(E)=Γ_0(E/1 TeV)ⁿ, tested in two forms: “state selection” (all eight off-identity entries Γ) and “phase perturbation.” The 90% CL limits at E_0=1 TeV are Γ_0<2.4×10⁻¹⁵, 4.6×10⁻¹⁶, 7.3×10⁻¹⁹ and 6.1×10⁻²¹ eV for n=0–3. Against the 2024 IceCube result (quoted at E_0=1 GeV), the gains are about 13× at n=2 and about 30× at n=3. At n=3 the limit falls below the natural expectation Γ_0=E_0ⁿ/M_Plⁿ⁻¹ for the first time, so a cubic-scaling effect would need extra suppression or a non-power-law form. The n=2 case matters most for theory, because it is the scaling found in string-motivated black-hole and D-foam calculations.

Caveats: - n=3 margin. Evaluating the paper’s formula at E_0=1 GeV gives about 6.7×10⁻³⁰ eV for the natural expectation, against a limit of 6.05×10⁻³⁰. That is a marginal crossing, not a deep exclusion. - n=0. The new limit is actually looser than 2024 (2.36 vs 1.17×10⁻¹⁵ eV). - Model assumptions. CPT conservation is assumed, since IceCube cannot separate ν from ν̅. The D matrix is diagonal, and decoherence is taken as independent of matter density. - Fit quality. Pre-unblinding goodness-of-fit p-values were only 4–5%.

arXiv:2610.17177 — MadNIS, Ready for Production at LO (Theo Heimel et al.)

MadNIS now covers full pp processes with all their partonic subprocesses, and it runs untuned from defaults set by a three-iteration VEGAS survey. It will be MadGraph7’s LO default. The main additions are: - learned sampling of symmetry permutations, and of flavour with a PDF prior; - merging of matrix elements, channels and, optionally, subprocesses; - buffered training on partially unweighted events; - concurrent training and generation on GPU.

On an H100 with training excluded (κ_∞), MadNIS beats VEGAS on every benchmark, by 1.27× (tt̅ dileptonic) up to 247× (ℓℓ+3j). Distributions match a sliced MG5aMC baseline in pulls, including the tails.

The amortization numbers the digest flagged look like this for tt̅+nj on an A100. Break-even with VEGAS comes at 9×10⁶, 1.5×10⁵ and 6×10³ events for n=1,2,3, after 8 s, 11 s and 1.4 min of training. At 10³ iterations, the speed-ups are already 2.9, 8.9 and 16.

Caveats: - Training cost of the headline numbers. The process-zoo figures come from trainings of up to 6.7–8.8 h. - Retraining. Any change of process, cuts or parameters requires a new training. - CPU. CPU training is more than 10× slower in wall-clock time. - Open choices. When to merge subprocesses is unresolved, and the defaults are “likely to evolve” (alpha release v0.2.1). - Low multiplicity. At low multiplicity, VEGAS combined with MadSpace mappings already captures most of the gain.

arXiv:2610.15248 — When hadrons collide: di-J/ψ structure in the final state (Eric S. Swanson (University of Pittsburgh))

Swanson gets a χ²/ndf=56/50 fit to the LHCb di-J/ψ spectrum (6.2–7.7 GeV) without introducing any states. The production model is a compact octet–octet ccc̅c̅ source in 2⁺⁺, rescattering through ten charmonium-pair channels. Quark-exchange kernels come from a constituent model whose parameters are fixed by the charmonium spectrum, and the scattering is solved to all orders with a Kohn–Hulthén–Kato resonating-group method.

The structures map onto thresholds: - a J/ψJ/ψ threshold enhancement in the X(6600) region; - a dip from flux lost to the J/ψψ(2S) channel, followed by a peak at 6.9 GeV; - a 7.2 GeV shoulder between the J/ψψ(3S) and ψ(2S)ψ(2S) thresholds.

Only three background parameters are free (a, c, λ), with DPS fixed to LHCb’s template. The fit needs both an incoherent remainder (c=0 gives 90/51) and a corrected continuum slope (λ=0 gives 152/51). The amplitude has poles at 6809-68i and 7102-57i MeV. Swanson argues these reflect a repulsive-shell/attractive-core interaction rather than tetraquarks.

Caveats: - CMS fit. CMS is fitted less well (117/55), and its dips are deeper than the model’s. - Missing and spurious features. The model undershoots the 6.9 GeV peak by 15–20% and predicts an unobserved ψ(2S)ψ(2S) bump near 7.4 GeV. - Omitted physics. Quark annihilation is left out, which removes absorption into D⁽)D̅⁽). J/ψψ(3770) is excluded because it couples only through tensor forces. - ΥΥ test. The prediction gives broad features at 19.3 and 19.7 GeV and a sharp dip near 20.05 GeV. Because an earlier loop-cusp model predicted the same enhancements, this tests threshold rescattering in general, not this model specifically.

item.title: Monday, October 12, 2026
item.description:
Freedman–McLerran, one order on

Kärkkäinen et al. arXiv:2610.13873 compute the full N³LO pressure of cold, dense QED. That problem has been open since the 1977 N²LO result, and the authors call it the first thermodynamic quantity at this order in a physical gauge theory. The series converges well. Their Bayesian estimate of missing orders, however, can exceed what scale variation suggests, which is the same warning as last week’s jet-veto N³LL result. Philcox’s two-loop galaxy power spectrum has a similar mixed outcome: the extra order buys reach in k but no gain on σ_8. BESIII supplies the day’s data, and the one LZ paper takes the solar bound as an input rather than ignoring it.

Themes

Next orders, mixed returns

  • Cold QED. Kärkkäinen et al. arXiv:2610.13873 are the obvious template for cold-quark-matter work.
  • Galaxy clustering. Philcox arXiv:2610.13867 extends the EFT of LSS to two loops in redshift space. That raises k_max from 0.2 to 0.34 h/Mpc, but 49 free coefficients absorb most of the new information.
  • Connection. Both extend this week’s perturbation-at-its-edges file. The pattern is that a higher order mainly tells you what the error budget actually was.

BESIII charmonium and charm

  • π⁰π⁰ threshold. BESIII arXiv:2610.13097 confirms the threshold structure in ψ(3686)→π⁰π⁰J/ψ at >10σ, with M=274.3 MeV and Γ=17.1 MeV. ChPT with final-state interactions fails at threshold, while the QCD multipole expansion with S–D mixing does better.
  • U-spin breaking. The companion amplitude analysis arXiv:2610.13101 finds U-spin-breaking magnitudes of 0.62–4.45 in D⁰→K_S,Lππ. This matters for the strong-phase inputs to γ.
  • Connection. These follow last week’s two BESIII Dalitz firsts.

ML across the analysis chain

  • Tokenizers. Krupa et al. arXiv:2610.13876 treat tokenization as rate-distortion. They get 4–11× compression with jet p_T resolution below 1%, and release heptokens. This picks up Godi et al.’s token-loss scaling from 10-02.
  • Fake taus. CMS arXiv:2610.13634 learns fake-tau factors from data with BDT reweighting.
  • Anomaly detection. Genovese et al. arXiv:2610.13437 add a local diagnostic that traces flagged events back to observables.
  • Agents and GPUs. HepUKE (Shang et al. arXiv:2610.12862) and Barik et al.’s Kokkos port of QCDLoop arXiv:2610.12627 round out the agent and GPU layers.

LZ via Dirac gauginos

Lee et al. arXiv:2610.13930 drop the Higgsino, which conflicts with the solar-neutrino bound they adopt. They use an R-symmetric Dirac bino with wino coannihilation and get 300–850 GeV spectra. Last week several LZ model papers skipped solar capture; this one is built around it.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.13873: A 49-year-old open order, closed. It also gives an honest uncertainty treatment that says scale bands understate the error.
  • arXiv:2610.13097: A 17-MeV-wide structure that ChPT cannot reproduce at threshold. Expect theory papers on what it is.
  • arXiv:2610.13867: A millisecond two-loop likelihood, plus a frank admission that σ_8 barely improves. Useful for calibrating two-loop expectations.
  • arXiv:2610.13634: Up to 70% less fake-tau systematic on Run 3 data. Anyone with a τ_h final state should check it.
  • arXiv:2610.13930: Turns the LZ splitting into a measurement of the anomaly-mediation scale (tens of MeV), with long-lived charged states as a collider handle.

From the community

  • arXiv:2610.12882 Undiscovering Quark-gluon Plasma — Thomas A. Trainor (hep-ph). A one-line abstract promises an essay on the scientific method in heavy-ion physics versus how large collaborations work. The title suggests it will be contrarian.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.13165 Recent results in b →s ℓℓ transitions at LHCb — Juan Jose Juan Castella (hep-ex). Proceedings, but they state that the K^*0μμ tensions persist at higher precision. That keeps the year’s C_9 question open.
  • arXiv:2610.12623 Probing τ lepton dipole moments at FCC-ee — Dario Buttazzo et al. (hep-ph). Statistical reach of |Δa_τ|<2.8×10⁻⁵, driven by γγ→ττ interference near threshold.
  • arXiv:2610.13633 nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions — nCTEQ Collaboration et al. (hep-ph). A new release using the largest dataset so far, with target-mass and deuteron corrections included.
  • arXiv:2610.12560 Quantum limit to transparency — Angelo Esposito et al. (hep-th). Photon decay to phonons sets an ω⁴ attenuation floor that remains even at zero temperature.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.13873 — Complete four-loop pressure of cold QED (Aapeli Kärkkäinen et al.)

The N³LO pressure of cold, dense massless QED (jellium setup) is now complete, the first new order since Freedman–McLerran in 1977. The soft and mixed sectors were already known, so the missing piece was the hard contribution: 10 four-loop 1PI vacuum diagrams at finite μ. The authors generated them in general R_ξ gauge and confirmed that the gauge dependence cancels. Canonicalization reduces O(10⁵⁾ scalar integrals to 75 masters, compared with 114 in QCD. The methods were: - cutting rules and self-energy techniques for the factorizable topologies, - IBP plus differential equations as a cross-check on a subset, - thermal loop-tree duality (LTD) Monte Carlo for roughly 70% of the integrals, at about 10⁶ CPU-core hours.

The hard IR pole cancels exactly against the mixed sector. The new constant term is p_3,5=1.02270(2)-5.64(5)N_f⁻¹⁻⁸.50(7)N_f⁻². Two independent checks hold up: - The Bugblatter sum gives b=-5.44(24)×10⁻⁷, against the literature value -5.545(12)×10⁻⁷. - Renormalization-group invariance holds through N³LO.

Along the way the authors corrected two errors in their earlier work: an O(ε) normalization error in the mixed term, and a factor of two in the N²LO handling that shifted p_3,4.

The physics result is the uncertainty story. At α_e=0.2, order-to-order shifts far exceed the X∈[1/2,2] scale band. The Bayesian abc error band at N²LO, by contrast, contains the actual N³LO result near its center, and the series stays predictive up to α_e≈0.4. Because the physical α is small, the direct phenomenology is negligible. The value is as a benchmark and as a partial integral library for cold quark matter, and hence for the neutron-star EoS. One caveat is that the Bayesian conclusion rests on modelling the coefficients as draws from a common distribution.

arXiv:2610.13097 — Threshold enhancement in π⁰π⁰ from ψ(3686)→π⁰π⁰J/ψ (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

BESIII selects 8.4×10⁶ events from 2.7×10⁹ ψ(3686) decays, using J/ψ→ee,μμ and a 7C kinematic fit. Background is about 0.1% and non-peaking. A Breit–Wigner fit to the threshold structure gives: - 2554 ± 62 signal events, at more than 10σ, - M=274.3±2.1±0.6 MeV, - Γ=17.1±1.5±0.5 MeV.

These values are consistent with the charged channel (about 283 MeV and 17 MeV). The neutral mode carries no I=1 component and no ISR background, which makes it the cleaner confirmation.

The unfolded 2D spectrum, in m_ππ and cosθ_π⁰, discriminates between models: - ChPT: adding FSI improves χ²/ndf from 48.6 to 6.5, but the model still misses the threshold region. - QCDME: with 2S–1D mixing fixed at θ_mix=12^∘ and FSI included, it describes the full spectrum. - Adler zero: the dip near 0.3 GeV persists, which BESIII ties to the Adler zero.

Caveats: - The mixing angle had to be fixed because it is strongly correlated with β. - A systematic trend remains in the cosθ pulls. - The ChPT parameter errors are implausibly tiny (e.g. g_1/g_0=-0.09426±0.00002). - The introduction says a structure near the π⁺π⁻ threshold would favor a rescattering cusp, but the paper never states whether the measured mass supports that reading. That question is left to theorists.

arXiv:2610.13867 — Redshift-space galaxy power spectrum at two loops (Oliver H. E. Philcox)

(The extracted text stops partway through the numerical section; the validation numbers below come from the abstract.)

Philcox gives the first complete two-loop, redshift-space galaxy P(k) in the EFT of large-scale structure (EFTofLSS). The model is renormalized at fifth order in fields and derivatives, and its ingredients are: - 17 leading-gradient, 7 next-to-leading-gradient and 1 next-to-next-to-leading-gradient bias operators, - spatially non-local counterterms generated by the dark-matter equations of motion, - 15 redshift-space counterterm combinations, - 6 stochastic terms.

That totals 49 coefficients, against 10 at one loop. Closure under renormalization is verified exactly at every power of f. IR resummation is applied without the usual factorized approximation. The same kernels fix the deterministic one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum, and 18 of the coefficients are constrained by the one-loop bispectrum.

The loop integrals are precomputed with vegas, so a likelihood evaluation takes milliseconds. On simulations, k_max rises from 0.2 to 0.34 h/Mpc for an LRG sample at z = 0.5. The new biases and counterterms absorb most of the added information, however, and σ_8 does not tighten appreciably. The author also stresses strong parameter degeneracies. On its own the result is a template and a calibration of two-loop expectations, not yet a cosmology gain. Its main promise is in joint fits with higher-order statistics.

(No full text was provided for the other two picks, CMS arXiv:2610.13634 and Lee et al. arXiv:2610.13930, so they are omitted here.)

item.title: Friday, October 9, 2026
item.description:
Three atmospheric detectors, one ordering

Jin et al. arXiv:2610.12208 fit public Super-K (pre-Gd), IceCube-DeepCore and six-unit KM3NeT/ORCA data jointly, with shared systematics correlated. They find Δχ²⁼¹¹.0 for normal ordering, and pseudo-experiments calibrate that to inverted ordering excluded at 3.3σ. Nine days ago JUNO reached 2.1σ only by leaning on long-baseline Δm²_31, so this is an independent route. It is a combination of public samples, though, not a collaboration result. Elsewhere, ATLAS reports s-channel single top at 5.1σ, phase transitions get firmer perturbative control, and the X(2370) glueball candidate faces a reanalysis that does not establish it.

Themes

Ordering and argon

Jin et al. arXiv:2610.12208 also report Δm²_31 at 2.2% and δ_CP=1.30⁺⁰.24_-0.28π, which they call competitive with accelerators. On the detector side, the SBND Collaboration et al. arXiv:2610.11782 report electron lifetime above 30 ms and wire noise at the theoretical floor, from the largest ν–Ar sample to date. Model-builders already treat normal ordering as input: Wang et al. arXiv:2610.11789 build post-JUNO seesaw textures. Strumia arXiv:2610.10696 gives textures for Koide plus Monday’s Alikhanov √2 relation.

Strong transitions, under control

This extends yesterday’s lattice first-order cluster. Gould et al. arXiv:2610.10692 build 3D EFTs for strong transitions, where standard dimensional reduction fails, and verify scale cancellation through NNLO. Bernardo et al. arXiv:2610.12284 find that thermal dimension-six operators barely move supercooled nucleation rates. Buschmann et al. arXiv:2610.12389 assemble many-bubble GW spectra from a library of two-bubble simulations, reaching boosts beyond direct lattice reach.

Charged LFV, ahead of Mu3e and conversion

This is new as a cluster. Di Lecce et al. arXiv:2610.10718 show that an accidental U(3)×CP in the composite sector aligns dipoles with Yukawas. That brings compositeness from ~100 TeV down to a few TeV, with μ→3e and μN→eN as the probes. Ali et al. arXiv:2610.12373 find that μ→e limits on τ-sector operator pairs beat direct τ bounds by 10–100s. That holds only if dimension-6 running and dimension-8 mixing are both kept. Calibbi et al. arXiv:2610.11839 supply the EFT review.

Amplitude machinery

Frederix et al.’s pyAmpliCol arXiv:2610.10729 packages last week’s symmetric-group FFT colour sums into a public UFO-capable generator with colour- and spin-correlated Borns. Bourjaily arXiv:2610.10672 gives pure two-loop masters with infrared regions isolated one-to-one, plus covariant massive BCFW arXiv:2610.10686.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.12208: 3.3σ normal ordering without any reactor input, the strongest ordering statement this season. The correlated-systematics treatment is the part to check.
  • arXiv:2610.11937: Dong et al. refit BESIII K_S⁰K_S⁰π⁰ with cross-channel interference and find no required X(2370). That undercuts the flavor-singlet glueball argument while last week’s glueball-vs-ϕh_1 question is still open.
  • arXiv:2610.11465: ATLAS observes s-channel single top at 5.1σ, using a GNN-based fit, with σ=10.8±2.2 pb, consistent with the SM.
  • arXiv:2610.10734: Schwartz et al. complete the NNLO 𝒩=4 EEC elliptic sector on the sunrise’s Γ_1(6) curve, “with AI under human supervision.” It is the LLMs-in-the-calculation thread’s most substantive entry yet.
  • arXiv:2610.10692: A systematically improvable framework for exactly the regime GW phenomenology cares about.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.10695 The Origin of the Fermi Halo-like Emission: A New Model of the Fermi Bubbles — Ilias Cholis et al. (astro-ph.HE). Totani’s halo emission is real, but Bubble substructure accounts for it, not dark-matter annihilation.
  • arXiv:2610.11035 Hamiltonian framework for Chiral Gauge Theories on a Disk Boundary — Srimoyee Sen (hep-lat). A Hamiltonian route to chiral gauge theories, a day after Craig’s lattice measure.
  • arXiv:2610.11121 Quantum Magic and the Strong Coupling Constant — Qiaofeng Liu et al. (hep-ph). Minimizing magic production gives α_s within 5%. The accompanying “quantum simulation” conjecture is the authors’, not a result.
  • arXiv:2610.09748 Cosmic Birefringence from Large Lepton Asymmetry — Kentaro Kasai et al. (astro-ph.CO). A neutrino-current route to the year’s birefringence signal, with an anisotropic signature to separate it from axion explanations.
  • arXiv:2610.12084 First demonstration of 50 ps four-dimensional vertex reconstruction with the Timepix4 beam telescope — David Bacher et al. (physics.ins-det). Vertex time resolution reaches 54 ps with no unexpected floor above that.
  • arXiv:2610.12443 A scalar-extended U(1)_L_μ-L_τ explanation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV excess — Dipankar Pradhan et al. (hep-ph). The day’s only LZ paper. The abstract does not mention solar capture.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.12208 — Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments (Miaochen Jin et al.)

Inverted ordering is excluded at 3.3σ using atmospheric data alone. Only 2 of 4397 IO pseudoexperiments exceed the observed χ²_IO-χ²_NO=11.0. The Clopper–Pearson 68% interval on that tail fraction gives Z∈[3.08,3.60]σ, and the more conservative CL_s gives 2.55σ. The ingredients are: - Super-K I–V (pure water), with an independent high-statistics GENIE Monte Carlo and a bug-fixed SK release confirmed by the collaboration. - IceCube-DeepCore, 8 years. - ORCA6.

Flux and cross-section nuisances (39 of 143) are shared across experiments. The individual preferences (Δχ²⁼⁶.2, 1.6, 0.5) add coherently via mantle/core MSW and parametric resonances at 2–10 GeV. Relative to a trivial χ² sum, the correlated treatment tightens Δm²_31 by 19% and sin²θ_23 by 9%. Results: Δm²_31=2.44⁺⁰.06_-0.04×10⁻³ eV² (2.2%), sin²θ_23=0.52 with Δχ²⁼⁰.3 between octants, and δ_CP=1.30⁺⁰.24_-0.28π (≈0.3π disfavoured at >2.7σ). The atmospheric contours sit closer to T2K than to NOvA. The authors estimate that adding JUNO’s Δm²_31 gives Δχ²≃16, near 4σ, but that figure still needs joint pseudoexperiments.

Caveats. - The overall goodness of fit is p=0.011, driven by ORCA6; it rises to 0.12 once finite Monte Carlo statistics are included. - The parameter goodness-of-fit test shows 2.2σ inter-experiment tension. IceCube and ORCA6 worsen by 13.7 and 9.6 in χ² at the combined best fit. - The shared CCQE normalization is pulled by −2.5σ. - θ_13 is fixed, and the ORCA energy-scale nuisance is absent. - The δ_CP constraint draws more on data residuals than on the Asimov expectation. - This is a combination of public data, not a collaboration result.

arXiv:2610.11937 — Reassessing the X(2370) in J/ψ→γK_S⁰K_S⁰π⁰ (Xiang-Kun Dong et al.)

A coherent coupled-channel fit does not require an X(2370) in K_S⁰K_S⁰π⁰. The fit uses a 12-channel K-matrix with dispersive loops, applied to digitized BESIII data: - two-dimensional mass maps (6264 KK bins and 6006 Kπ bins); - the parent-mass spectrum.

Adding an eighth bare state near 2.37 GeV lowers the deviance by only 1.26% (7926.4→7826.6, with 16 extra parameters), and the projected line shapes are nearly identical. The extra pole sits at 2424-i 149 MeV, twice as broad as the PDG reference 2377-i 74. Its identification with X(2370) is unclear.

The physics consequence is for the flavor-singlet argument. If the true X(2370)→KK̅π yield is smaller than the 1D fits imply, the denominator of BESIII’s ℛ<0.081 shrinks. The small K^*K̅ yield would then no longer demonstrate selective suppression, which weakens the glueball and η_c-analogy readings without excluding them.

Caveats, stated by the authors. - Bin contents are reconstructed from a colour palette, with no inter-distribution correlations, efficiency, or resolution. - No significance or pole uncertainties are quoted. - Only mesonic channels are modelled, so the ΣΣ̅ interpretation is not tested. - K_0^*(1430) parameters were tuned within their uncertainties. - The J/ψ→K^*0K̅^*0 background is not modelled.

arXiv:2610.11465 — Observation of s-channel single top-quark production at 13 TeV with ATLAS (ATLAS Collaboration)

(Abstract only.) ATLAS reports the first single-experiment observation of s-channel single top, at 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected). The dataset is 140 fb⁻¹, with events selected for exactly one lepton, missing E_T, and exactly two b-jets. A GNN separates the signal from tt̅, W+jets and t-channel backgrounds, and a likelihood fit to its output gives σ_tb̅+t̅b=10.8±1.5 (stat)±1.6 (syst) pb, consistent with the SM. The comparable statistical and systematic errors suggest further gains will need systematic reductions as well as more data. The abstract does not quote the SM prediction or a |V_tb| interpretation.

Citation radar

The radar this week is dominated by one hook: the single LZ nuclear recoil near 248 keV. That one event is generating its own literature, which tells you the community treats a 2.6σ, background-free curiosity as worth building models around. The papers collecting citations are the ones that give everyone a concrete scenario to point at.

arXiv:2609.07811 — Higgsino Dark Matter Interpretation of the LZ High-Recoil Event in the GNMSSM with TeV-Scale Gauginos (Subhadip Bisal et al.)

Bisal, Cao and Li interpret the LZ event as endothermic, Z-mediated Higgsino up-scattering, χ̃₁⁰N→χ̃₂⁰N. In the MSSM, a ~350 keV splitting needs |M₁,₂|~10⁶–10⁷ GeV or a Bino–Wino cancellation tuned to ~10⁻⁴. In the GNMSSM, Higgsino–Singlino mixing adds an independent contribution ∝λ²v²/(dμ_tot) that cancels the gaugino term.

The paper presents six benchmarks from the authors’ earlier scan, with these properties: - m_χ ≈ 660–1110 GeV and δ = 333–350 keV. - |M₁,₂| = 2–5 TeV, with both signs of M₁M₂ represented. - Ωh² within a few percent of the measured value. - Δχ² < 1 under the Standard Halo Model in every case, best 0.03.

The authors are candid on two limits. The tuning is relocated, not removed: Δ_FT exceeds 5×10³ at every point. The IceCube bound of δ ≳ 566 keV remains open, and the provided text cuts off before their singlet-resonance evasion is worked out.

The paper has drawn 49 citations since its 7 September posting. That likely reflects the LZ-event wave rather than a decisive result; the introduction alone cites ~40 interpretation papers. Its value as a citation is practical: explicit benchmarks with neutralino masses quoted to six significant digits make it the convenient reference for “the singlet-extended Higgsino option.”

item.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026
item.description:
A lattice measure for chiral gauge theories

Craig arXiv:2610.09093 constructs a gauge-invariant measure for overlap fermions nonperturbatively, in a class of nonabelian chiral gauge theories that includes the SM. He calls the result “a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model.” The construction holds on admissible gauge fields and goes through Lüscher’s reconstruction, so it falls short of a simulation recipe. Still, it is the most consequential claim of the day. Elsewhere, LZ-2024 closes a door that has nothing to do with the 248 keV event. Lattice phase-transition papers also cluster, which is relevant to Pisarski’s open question on chiral transition order.

Themes

LZ, a null and two fits

Bao et al. arXiv:2610.10219 find that LZ-2024 excludes sub-100 GeV Bino dark matter via h- and Z-resonances at >5.9σ and >4.1σ. This holds even with adverse 3σ FLAG shifts, partial dark-matter fractions and no LHC input. On the recoil, Lian et al. arXiv:2610.09753 argue that Higgsino-pair inelastic fits overproduce solar neutrinos, while singlino ground states survive. That turns the solar bound from veto into composition probe. Sheikh et al. arXiv:2610.09516 get an excited fraction near ½ from thermal quasi-pNGBs, which is the exothermic regime Oliveira flagged on 09-29.

First-order transitions on lattices

  • Kitajima et al. arXiv:2610.09257 find that Chern-Simons production survives strong supercooling in 3D bubble-collision simulations. That keeps cold baryogenesis alive where entropy dilution would otherwise kill it.
  • Li et al. arXiv:2610.09325 add scalar metric perturbations to such simulations for the first time. They find these sources can exceed ⅓ of the scalar-field gravitational-wave signal on superhorizon scales.
  • Goswami et al. arXiv:2610.10350 derive the leading finite-size correction for Z(2) and O(2) models in a field. It removes a systematic in 2+1 T_χ extrapolations, the same data Pisarski proposed testing against.

Perturbation theory at its edges

  • Marino et al. arXiv:2610.10059 show that the pole-mass renormalon in large-N Gross–Neveu is cured by nonperturbative trans-series terms. That is timely after last week’s −216 MeV top-mass relation shift.
  • Boito et al. arXiv:2610.09874 estimate the α_s⁷ term of H→gg using Padé approximants.
  • Fang et al. arXiv:2610.09680 put NNLO ISR for μμγ into McMule.
  • Jerala et al. arXiv:2610.08950 make electroweak Sudakov reweighting resonance-aware for FxFx samples. They state plainly that it is not full NLO EW.

Detector physics from first principles

  • Riegler arXiv:2610.09961 derives Green’s functions and weighting fields for arbitrary dielectric multilayers.
  • Hammann et al. arXiv:2610.10161 resolve xenon NIR scintillation in 12 bands. The slow continuum points to an ionic-dimer transition with a ~3 μs lifetime.
  • Bacher et al. arXiv:2610.10328 match fit-based Timepix4 timewalk resolution using a small network and 20% of the calibration data.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.09093: Lattice chiral gauge theory has been stuck on the measure for decades. A claimed SM-inclusive construction is worth reading for exactly where “admissible” bites.
  • arXiv:2610.10219: A conservatively framed null that removes light resonant Binos from the MSSM menu, using one-loop vertex corrections of up to 50%.
  • arXiv:2610.09753: The clearest statement yet that swapping ground and excited states preserves the LZ spectrum while moving solar annihilation by orders of magnitude.
  • arXiv:2610.10059: A solvable model in which the pole-mass ambiguity is cancelled explicitly. It also identifies the on-shell corrections that the condensate OPE misses.
  • arXiv:2610.09874: Gives -312±15 for the unknown coefficient, validated by postdiction and a large-n_f constraint. The estimate cuts scale dependence by ~1.5×.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.09626 Observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz transition J/ψ→e⁺e⁻η_c — BESIII Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). The ratio to γη_c is R=0.65(7)% and the form factors agree with theory. This is the second BESIII Dalitz first in two days.
  • arXiv:2610.10016 Two-pion exchange potential in D⁽)D⁽) system — Daiki Suenaga et al. (hep-ph). N²LO triangle diagrams reproduce the HAL QCD (e⁻m_πr/r)² tail.
  • arXiv:2610.10185 Search prospect for electrophilic bosons at the μTRISTAN — Amit Adhikary et al. (hep-ph). Projects up to four orders of magnitude improvement for electrophilic ALPs.
  • arXiv:2610.09592 Boson-Fermion Atomic Dark Matter — Natsumi Nagata et al. (hep-ph). Atom–antiatom oscillations make asymmetric DM symmetric today, with ΔN_eff≃0.05–0.07.
  • arXiv:2610.09751 SMEFT Constraints via Quantum Entanglement in Portal-Mediated Scattering — Shilpa Jangid et al. (hep-ph). Argues entanglement entropies are linear in 1/Λ², though the abstract gives no quantitative sensitivity.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.09093 — A gauge-invariant measure for lattice chiral fermions (Nathaniel Craig)

Craig claims a nonperturbative, smooth, exponentially local, gauge-invariant overlap-fermion measure for SU(5) with 10⊕5̅. He extends it to all four global forms [SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1)]/Γ_SM, Γ_SM=1,ℤ_2,ℤ_3,ℤ_6, by embedding SM links into SU(5).

The key move replaces Lüscher’s abelian interpolation of the gauge potential to zero, which can exit the admissible domain for nonabelian fields. Instead:

  • A smooth connection is reconstructed from U and sampled at auxiliary spacings h_n=3⁻ⁿ, with fine plaquettes obeying 1-(F_hU)(p)≤Cεh².
  • Hermitian Wilson operators at successive spacings are interpolated linearly. The intermediate operators are not link fields, and a uniform gap g is proved throughout.
  • Each step contributes a curvature-strip term B_n, and the measure term is 𝔏=∑_n B_n.
  • Return phases telescope. An exact colour-trace identity for 10⊕5̅ cancels the leading terms, which makes the sum converge.
  • Global integrability on noncontractible loops uses an auxiliary SU(3) connection under which the fermions pair conjugately.

The general sufficient conditions are cubic-anomaly cancellation plus even multiplicity of half-integer-isospin representations under an SU(2)⊂SU(N_c). The author says the latter is an artefact of the method.

Where “admissible” bites: - The construction requires a sufficiently small plaquette bound ε. It is volume-independent but not quantified in the extracted text. - The measure is fixed only up to one constant phase per connected component of admissible fields. The current’s transformation laws do not guarantee that every choice of these relative phases respects discrete symmetries.

The convergence, locality and gap estimates sit in appendices not included in the extract. Lean verification is relegated to supplementary material. As the digest notes, this is an existence construction, not a simulation algorithm.

arXiv:2610.10219 — Is the Light Neutralino Dark Matter Still Viable in the MSSM After the LZ-2024 Results? (Zhiyang Bao et al.)

LZ-2024 excludes the sub-100 GeV Bino h-funnel at Z>5.9 (p=1.8×10⁻⁹) and the Z-funnel at Z>4.1 (p=2.1×10⁻⁵). The result holds for Ωh²⁼⁰.12 and for 0.06 (half the dark matter), without imposing the LHC bound μ≳760 GeV.

The argument rests on one coupling (C_h or C_Z) setting both annihilation and scattering. Finite mediator width and thermal smearing cap ⟨σv⟩, so the relic density imposes a floor on σ^SI or σ^SD_n.

The analysis is deliberately conservative: - Loop corrections: full one-loop vertex corrections (904 diagrams) give K^SI≲1.5 and K^SD_n≲1.3. Scale variation changes these corrections by at most 5%. - Hadronic inputs: FLAG-2024 values (σ_πN=42.2±2.4 MeV) are used, with worst-case 3σ rescalings of 0.78 (SI) and 0.62 (SD) applied at every point. The authors note that the Roy–Steiner value σ_πN≃58–59 MeV would only raise σ^SI.

The resulting cross-section floors sit nearly an order of magnitude above the LZ-2024 limits. LZ-2022 gave only Z<2.

Caveats: - The LZ-2024 recast is micrOMEGAs’ background-free Poisson model. It is calibrated near 90% CL and then extrapolated far into the tail. - DDCalc implements only LZ-2022. There, micrOMEGAs underestimates Z, which supports the claim that the micrOMEGAs numbers are conservative. - Near-degenerate Higgsino–Wino points (splitting <3 GeV) were cut for counterterm instability.

What remains for a thermal Bino is coannihilation, heavy-Higgs resonance or well-tempering, which together point to |m_χ̃|≳200 GeV.

arXiv:2610.09753 — Can Nuclear Recoils and Solar Neutrinos Resolve the Composition of Singlino-Higgsino Dark Matter? (Jingwei Lian et al.)

Abstract only. The paper’s point is a degeneracy: swapping ground and excited states can leave an inelastic recoil spectrum unchanged while shifting ground-state annihilation by orders of magnitude. Solar-neutrino signals from captured dark matter then distinguish compositions that recoils cannot.

Applied in the NMSSM to fits of the high-energy LZ candidate, the analysis finds: - Disfavoured: Higgsino-pair inelastic fits overproduce solar signals. - Solar-compatible: singlino ground states, and Higgsino ground states with weak inelastic transitions. - Escape route: an elastic Higgsino alternative evades the solar bound by closing the inelastic transition that drives capture.

The abstract gives no quantitative limits. The authors acknowledge residual degeneracies tied to annihilation, halo and detector assumptions.

item.title: Wednesday, October 7, 2026
item.description:
Three bids for the B_s1

Two more groups interpret LHCb’s B_s0^(5700) today. With last week’s Albaladejo et al., all three now place the 1⁺ partner between 5740 and 5755 MeV. That agreement says less than it seems. Albaladejo already noted that the 1⁺–0⁺ splitting essentially equals the B_s^–B_s difference, so the partner mass is nearly fixed by heavy-quark spin symmetry. The models actually differ on widths and on how much of the state is a bare bs̅ core. The rest of the day is spectroscopy-heavy, with steady precision inputs and one LZ paper.

Themes

Molecular dressing of the B_s0^*

Hao et al. arXiv:2610.07106 find that a compact quark model overshoots the mass by ~120 MeV. Adding BK coupled channels pulls the pole to ~5727 MeV and explains the narrow width. Sánchez-Illana et al. arXiv:2610.07171 work in the hidden-gauge formalism and predict five further states. A bare component cuts the B_s⁰π⁰ width from 50 keV to 10–20 keV. Albaladejo’s models gave 34–82.5 keV, so the isospin-violating width is now the discriminating number. Kinugawa et al. arXiv:2610.08340 add the general theory of how Coulomb interactions modify compositeness universality near threshold.

Multiquark methods, and a glueball radius

Zhang et al. arXiv:2610.07818 diagonalize a potential model exactly on a lattice. Note that this is a discretized quark model, not lattice QCD. They find a ccc̅c̅ 0⁺ state 33 MeV below η_cη_c and claim it is robust against the choice of potential. Jiang et al. arXiv:2610.06979 read X(3790) and G(3900) as P-wave DD̅⁽*) configurations. Mamo arXiv:2610.08545 gives the first holographic glueball gravitational form factors. The scalar Breit mass radius of 0.276 fm sits close to Issifu et al.’s 0.28 fm from last Thursday, though the radius definitions may differ.

Perturbative inputs for the next machine

Maier et al. arXiv:2610.08282 compute four-loop top-mediated QCD corrections to Δr and Δκ. The resulting m_W shift is a few hundred keV, which the authors call relevant at FCC-ee. Guzzi et al. arXiv:2610.07233 lay out CT’s route to partial-N³LO fits. Their evolution still uses approximate four-loop splitting functions. Chen et al. arXiv:2610.07145 resum the back-to-back EEC plateau through N³LL in 𝒩=4 SYM and interpolate it to strong coupling. They do this with a “human-in-the-loop agentic workflow,” another entry in last week’s LLMs-inside-the-calculation thread.

Fast, but not lossy

Pizzichemi et al.’s HybridMC arXiv:2610.08054 parametrizes optical transport for LHCb’s ECAL Upgrade II and gains a factor of 150–480 in speed. The authors explicitly position it against generative flash sims, which cannot reproduce the photon arrival times that tens-of-ps timing needs. This is a useful counterpoint to the surrogate enthusiasm of 09-28. Bustamante’s Magnus arXiv:2610.07159 covers the oscillation side.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2610.07106: Shows quantitatively why the compact picture fails by ~120 MeV. It names B_s1(5747) and its radiative modes as the Run 3 test.
  • arXiv:2610.07818: A deeply bound, strong-decay-stable fully charmed tetraquark is a bold claim. Worth reading to see how much weight “exact diagonalization” can carry inside a potential model.
  • arXiv:2610.08282: A four-loop electroweak-relation input that FCC-ee m_W projections will need.
  • arXiv:2610.07159: Magnus is a Magnus-expansion oscillation solver for any Hermitian Hamiltonian, flavor count and density profile. It is the fastest high-accuracy public code among those the author compared, and likely to be widely adopted.
  • arXiv:2610.07150: Craig et al. show the electroweak anomaly alone induces ΔB=ΔL∈3ℤ in monopole–fermion scattering, even with B and L classically conserved.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2610.08606 Missing Mass Matters: Neutrinophilic Scalar in D-Meson Decays — Jin-Man Cai et al. (hep-ph). Modelling the M²_miss distribution makes the D⁺ bound substantially weaker than prior estimates. File it under corrections the size of errors.
  • arXiv:2610.07493 Neutral Pseudoscalar Mesons, Hadron Light-by-Light Scattering, and the Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment — Cong-Cong Ye et al. (hep-ph). Finds π⁰⁺η+η’ poles at 84.3(0.8)×10⁻¹¹, lower than some estimates. The authors argue the pole term is not known to better than 5%.
  • arXiv:2610.08648 Testing Dark Matter Coscattering with the High-Energy LZ Recoil — Sreemanti Chakraborti et al. (hep-ph). The day’s only LZ paper: dark-photon-enhanced singlet–doublet DM at 750 GeV–1.6 TeV with a ~100 keV splitting. The abstract does not address solar capture.
  • arXiv:2610.07054 First observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay ψ(3686)→μ⁺μ⁻η’ — BESIII Collaboration et al. (hep-ex). Observed at 6.1σ and consistent with vector meson dominance; no lepton-universality violation.
  • arXiv:2610.07155 Coherent versus incoherent amplification… — Clemente Smarra et al. (hep-ph). Reconciles the g_aγ and g_aγ² scalings of stimulated axion decay through the axion coherence length.

Deep dives

arXiv:2610.07106 — Molecular Structure Effects in Low-Lying P-wave Bottom-Strange Meson Spectrum (Wei Hao et al.)

A compact bs̅ picture cannot reach the B_s0^*(5700): the plain confinement+OGE model puts the 0⁺ at 5851 MeV. One-loop (α_s²) corrections to the OGE potential lower it only to 5816 MeV, still ~120 MeV above LHCb’s 5698.9±1.5±0.6 MeV. Coupling the bare state to BK/B^*K via ³P_0 vertices supplies the missing shift and brings the 0⁺ to 5727 MeV, within ~30 MeV of data. Near-threshold phase-space suppression accounts for the narrow width. The same machinery puts the 1⁺ partner at 5755 MeV (B^K-dominated), close to Nowak–Zahed’s chiral-doubling 5747±2 MeV. The j_ℓ=3/2 states stay essentially compact. The authors give E1 widths of 45 keV for B_s0^→Bs^*γ and ~55–58 keV for the 1⁺→Bs⁽*)γ modes, which they propose as the Run 3 discovery channels.

Caveats: - Molecular content not quantified. The paper does not report a B_s⁰π⁰ width. That is today’s discriminating number against Albaladejo et al. and Sánchez-Illana et al. It also gives no explicit compositeness, despite promising to quantify the admixture. - Radiative widths may be mislabeled. The quoted 58/55 keV values come from the Table 4 rows for B’_s1(1P). The B_s1(1P) rows, which correspond to the state assigned to 5747 in Table 3, give 50.9/34.6 keV. - Bare-state wavefunctions. All radiative widths use quark-model wavefunctions, not the dressed ones. - B_s2^ width is a fit, not a test.The ³P_0 strengtγ_0 was fitted to the B_s2^*(5840) width, so reproducing its 1.5 MeV is not an independent check. - Residual offset. The 0⁺ still misses by ~30 MeV.

arXiv:2610.07818 — Fully charmed tetraquarks on the Lattice with controlled errors (Zhenyu Zhang et al.)

The headline result is a J^P=0⁺ ccc̅c̅ state at 5934.8(13) MeV, 33.2(13) MeV below η_cη_c, and therefore strong-decay-stable. The authors discretize a standard OGE+linear potential model on a periodic lattice and diagonalize it with Lanczos (“LQPM”). This is a lattice-discretized quark model, not lattice QCD. Benchmarks are good: - η_c, J/ψ and the 2S states land within a few MeV of experiment. - Ω_ccc=4817.3(9) MeV agrees with NNQS and lies below the variational GEM value of 4823.

They also find a 1⁺ only 10.9 MeV below η_cJ/ψ, which they flag as potential-dependent. The 2⁺ sits 24 MeV above J/ψJ/ψ, and they connect it to the CMS near-threshold 2⁺ structure. A bound 0⁺ contradicts essentially every prior model, including DeepQuark. The authors attribute their ~500 MeV lower masses to enforcing full antisymmetry with non-symmetric spatial parts. Restricting to symmetric spatial functions recovers NNQS (~6414–6508 MeV).

The “controlled errors” claim deserves scrutiny: - Coarse spacing. The tetraquark is computed at a≈0.2 fm, a spacing at which the supplement says charmonium has not converged. Finer spacings “do not converge.” - Threshold mismatch. The quoted 5968 MeV threshold equals twice the fine-lattice η_c mass. The text does not show it evaluated at a≈0.2 fm. - Small boxes, poor fits. Only five boxes are used, up to 1.8 fm. The extrapolation adds 16 MeV beyond the largest box, and the fits have χ²/dof=15–28. The ±1.3 MeV error is fit-only. - Scattering-like color structure. The color ratio converges to the 2:1 value characteristic of meson–meson scattering states.

arXiv:2610.08282 — Relations between electroweak parameters to order α_s³ (Andreas Maier et al.)

Maier and Marquard complete the top-mediated four-loop QCD corrections to Δr̅ and Δκ beyond the leading Δρ term. They supply the missing pieces: - the four-loop flavour-singlet polarization functions; - top-mass corrections to the bb correlator; - a sixth low-energy term in the axial correlator.

The expansion in M_Z²/m_t² is taken to M_Z¹⁰/m_t¹⁰, with negligible truncation error. The new α_s³ m_t^≤0 terms shift M_W by ≈ −0.8 MeV with an on-shell top mass and ≈ −0.2 MeV in MS. For comparison, FCC-ee projects 0.16 MeV systematic and 0.18 MeV statistical uncertainty, so these terms are relevant at that precision.

Two points matter for projections: - Scheme dependence. In MS the subleading α_s³m̅_t⁰ term (−0.22 MeV) exceeds the formally leading α_s³m̅_t² term (−0.03 MeV). The factor-of-four scheme spread at this order is itself a theory uncertainty at the FCC-ee scale. - Five loops needed. Extrapolating the on-shell pattern, the authors expect α_s⁴ M_t² to contribute several hundred keV. That makes five-loop ρ desirable.

Scope is pure QCD on top/bottom loops, and the numerical study neglects the Δr–Δr̅ difference. Results are supplied in electronic form.

item.title: Tuesday, October 6, 2026
item.description:
Red dwarfs reject the G-step

Sakstein et al. arXiv:2610.04048 test Hubble-tension fixes that change Newton’s constant abruptly in the recent past. They use fully convective red dwarfs, whose thermal timescales match the proposed look-back times, and eight eclipsing-binary mass-radius measurements.
