  • arXiv:2609.16342 Top-quark pair production sensitivity at the FCC-ee — De Piccoli et al. (hep-ph) — matrix-element SMEFT discriminants reaching 30 TeV single-operator; the EFT-default thread again.
  • arXiv:2609.16292 Υ(nS) in O+O collisions — Thapa et al. (nucl-th) — sequential suppression predictions for the Run 3 oxygen program.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.17267 — Non-singlet splitting functions at four loops (Thomas Gehrmann et al.)

The full non-singlet splitting functions P_ns⁺, P_ns⁻, and P_ns^s=P_ns^v-P_ns⁻ are now known analytically at four loops for arbitrary Mellin moment n — the reference the field will cite for N³LO evolution. The method computes off-shell quark operator matrix elements for twist-two spin-n operators, using generating functions to keep n arbitrary while retaining standard IBP identities (via Qgraf, Form, Reduze2, and the finite-field Finred code). Rather than fight the elliptic geometries appearing in one color sector, the differential equations in the tracing parameter t are Taylor-expanded about t=0, where the integrals reduce to known four-loop propagator masters; moments up to n∼4000 are then generated and the all-n result reconstructed from an ansatz of harmonic sums up to weight 7. Results confirm all known color coefficients and reproduce independent fixed-moment checks, the four-loop cusp coefficient A_q⁽⁴⁾, and yield fully analytic virtual anomalous dimensions B_q⁽⁴⁾ and B_g⁽⁴⁾ plus the eikonal soft anomalous dimension f_r⁽⁴⁾.

Why it matters: consistent N³LO LHC cross sections require exactly these functions, previously available only as numerical approximations or partial analytics — anchoring today’s precision-QCD theme. Agreement with the Moch–Ruijl–Ueda–Vermaseren–Vogt numerics is good, though P_ns⁽³⁾,+ sits slightly above their error band at small x. One honest wrinkle: the ln⁴ x small-x terms disagree with the resummation prediction of Davies et al., by a piece subleading in N_c and proportional to ζ_2 — possibly an (iπ)² phase effect the authors flag for investigation. The singlet case remains, requiring gauge-variant operator renormalization.

arXiv:2609.16219 — Enhanced Standard Model bound on charm CP violation from QCD penguins (Ali Mohamed et al.)

Using light-cone sum rules with an auxiliary momentum inserted at the weak vertex (following the B→ππ methodology of Khodjamirian) to avoid parasitic cuts, Mohamed and Piscopo compute for the first time the QCD-penguin operator matrix elements for D⁰→K⁺K⁻ and D⁰→π⁺π⁻ at leading order in α_s. The scalar penguins Q_5,Q_6 are strongly enhanced: -i⟨Q_6⟩_ππ=2.09 GeV³ versus 0.228 for the current-current Q_1^d — roughly a factor of ten. Two sources drive this: quark-condensate contributions arising at tree level (enhanced by 16π² over the loop-induced terms) and an annihilation-type contribution from the u̅ u component entering already at twist three. Recomputed current-current matrix elements agree with the earlier Lenz et al. determination to within 5–10%, and the resulting branching ratios (ℬ(ππ)=1.22×10⁻³, ℬ(KK)=2.44×10⁻³) match HFLAV within their ~100% uncertainties.

Why it matters: the 2019 LHCb ΔA_CP∼10⁻³ needs penguin-to-tree ratios of order unity, an order of magnitude above naive estimates, and whether this fits the SM hinges on hadronic matrix elements. Enhanced penguins narrow the SM-vs-experiment gap — direct progress on the standing charm-CPV puzzle flagged in August. Caveat, stated plainly: the strong phases remain unconstrained at LO α_s, so no quantitative CP-asymmetry prediction follows; the bound assumes maximal phases. The annihilation approximation carries an expected ≥30% error because s_0/m_D²∼20–30% (versus ~3% for B decays).

arXiv:2609.16120 — Dark Radiation Sticks Together: Dark QCD and the Hubble Tension (Matthew R. Buckley et al.)

Buckley, Fernandez, and Putney propose a confining SU(N_c) dark sector with heavy stable quarks (the dark matter) and light quarks whose confinement at Λ_D∼ MeV turns the dark radiation into light dark pions. Crucially, residual strong interactions make this radiation a viscous imperfect fluid rather than free-streaming — modeled in a modified CLASS with drag (Γ_drag) and relaxation-time equations. The viscosity suppresses high-ℓ CMB oscillations relative to free-streaming ΔN_eff, letting the model raise H_0 without spoiling the high-ℓ multipoles or S_8. A full MCMC over Planck, ACT, DESI DR2, Pantheon+, SH0ES, and BBN yields H_0=71.60±0.63 km/s/Mpc with a residual tension of ∼3σ (Q_DMAP=3.0σ vs 6.0σ for ΛCDM), competitive with Hubble World Cup “finalists.” It also fits DESI BAO better than Planck-only ΛCDM.

Why it matters: this is a genuinely different mechanism for the Hubble tension — not just extra N_eff, but self-interacting radiation whose fluid behavior evades the high-ℓ constraints that cap free-streaming models near 4σ. The large late-time self-interaction cross section (∼Λ_D⁻²) evades Bullet Cluster bounds because hard momentum transfer requires perturbative heavy-quark scattering. Honest caveats: the best-fit Λ_D∼1 MeV produces dark acoustic oscillations in tension with Lyman-α, though Λ_D≳3–5 MeV evades this with negligible fit degradation; and the CLASS modifications were partly LLM-generated.

item.title: Tuesday, September 15, 2026
item.description:
The xenon event meets its adjudicators

Four weeks on, the LZ recoil still owns roughly a sixth of the listings, but the register has shifted again — from fits, to bounds, to concrete discriminators. Two papers today try to end arguments rather than start them: Ghosh et al. arXiv:2609.15321 show that no plausible halo modeling rescues the thermal higgsino from solar capture, and Baer et al. arXiv:2609.15782 argue argon settles the endothermic-vs-exothermic question outright. The day’s genuine breadth, though, sits away from xenon — a clean BESIII lepton-universality test, a precision-QCD stack running from polarized SIDIS to the proton–neutron mass difference, and quantum information reaching small-x saturation.

Themes

The LZ event, now sorted by test rather than model

The model zoo keeps refilling — radiative Dirac neutrino mass (Borah et al. arXiv:2609.15027), hidden U(1) scalars (arXiv:2609.15600, He et al. arXiv:2609.15714), sneutrinos (Lian et al. arXiv:2609.15742), neutron disappearance (Uttayarat et al. arXiv:2609.15933), even modified gravity (Barman arXiv:2609.15118) and KK gravitons (Le-Yaouanc et al. arXiv:2609.15413). But the useful papers are discriminators: Ghosh et al. arXiv:2609.15321 close the astrophysical escape hatch for the higgsino, Baer et al. arXiv:2609.15782 and Ahmed et al. arXiv:2609.15634 turn target choice and xenon isotopes into kinematic filters, and Palmisano et al. arXiv:2609.15985 and Mahapatra et al. arXiv:2609.14799 map the full posterior and show boosted vs inelastic readings are spectrally separable. This is the falsifiability pivot the memory has tracked for three weeks, now the dominant mode.

Precision flavor at BESIII and LHCb

BESIII delivers the first observation of D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ arXiv:2609.15655, with a μ/e ratio of 0.92±0.13±0.08 — lepton universality intact — and the most precise D_s→f_0(980) form factor to date. LHCb reports the first observation of Ξ_b⁰→Ξ⁰ J/ψ arXiv:2609.15251, notable for the first full Ξ⁰ reconstruction at an LHC experiment. Add improved η’→3π amplitude analyses arXiv:2609.15053 and BESIII cross-section scans; the consolidating-null flavor picture from August holds.

Nucleon structure and the precision-QCD stack

A dense structure day: first N³LO polarized SIDIS (Dong et al. arXiv:2609.13743), a dispersive sum rule cutting the isovector-polarizability uncertainty fourfold and pinning δm_QED=0.71 MeV (Cao et al. arXiv:2609.15154), NNPDF4.1 progress arXiv:2609.15574, a GPD review arXiv:2609.15583, and several small-x TMD/CGC papers. Two stand out conceptually: Fucilla et al. arXiv:2609.14700 connect spin-spin entanglement and Bell nonlocality to Pomeron and saturation physics, extending the collider-QI program into small-x; and Lee et al. arXiv:2609.13366 recast the heavy-quark forward-backward asymmetry as an electroweak anomaly via “flavor flux correlators,” computed to N³LO.

ML in the detector plumbing

The autodiff/ML wave keeps colonizing the plumbing: knowledge distillation of a normalizing flow into FPGA firmware for the CMS L1 trigger (Abson et al. arXiv:2609.15295), ML calibration of CMS EM showers arXiv:2609.15377, density-guided neural processes for efficiency estimation on MAJORANA data arXiv:2609.13593, and a finite-Asimov construction for neural SBI arXiv:2609.14136.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.15321 — Ghosh et al.: halo modeling, including LMC-aware N-body sims, cannot reconcile the higgsino with solar capture. The astrophysical escape route is now closed.
  • arXiv:2609.15782 — Baer et al.: argon predicts a 336 keV line (endothermic) or nothing (exothermic), and DEAP-3600 already has the exposure. The cleanest single test proposed yet.
  • arXiv:2609.15655 — BESIII’s first D_s⁺→f_0(980)μν, an LFU check and the most precise D_s→f_0 form factor.
  • arXiv:2609.14700 — Fucilla et al. tie quark-pair entanglement and Bell nonlocality to saturation observables; the QI program reaching small-x.
  • arXiv:2609.13366 — Lee et al.’s flavor flux correlators, reframing A_FB as an anomaly and computing it to N³LO with archival e⁺e⁻ data in mind.

From the community

The DPF’s formal comment to the SCAC facilities subcommittee arXiv:2609.15401 Comment for the SCAC Facilities Subcommittee from the Division of Particles and Fields — Akerib et al. (hep-ex) lays out the field’s case for DUNE Phase II detectors and a U.S. Higgs-factory contribution, anchored to the P5 plan — worth a read for anyone tracking U.S. collider strategy.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.15154 Precision Sum Rule for Nucleon Isovector Polarizabilities and the Proton-Neutron Mass Difference — Cao et al. (hep-ph) — a fourfold-tighter δm_QED and a low-energy test of Reggeon dominance.
  • arXiv:2609.15251 Observation of Ξ_b⁰→Ξ⁰ J/ψ — LHCb (hep-ex) — first full Ξ⁰ reconstruction at the LHC.
  • arXiv:2609.15026 *Vacuum Polarization from Dark Fermion Loops in Z’ Models and B→K^μμ — Gupta et al. (hep-ph) — a Z’-portal fit driving ΔC_9≃-1.2; the C_9 thread still alive.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.15321 — Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with Astrophysical Uncertainties and Solar Capture (Aditya Ghosh et al.)

The higgsino reading of LZ’s 248 keV recoil cannot survive the solar-capture bound no matter how the halo is stretched. Ghosh, Chavez, and Kelso compute the expected LZ signal for a 1.1 TeV thermal higgsino (WimPyDD, including the factor-4 cross-section correction of Pospelov–Ramani) across the full Standard Halo Model parameter space and, separately, using N-body hydrodynamical halos that include the LMC’s imprint on the high-speed tail. IceCube/Super-K non-observation of solar annihilation neutrinos requires the inelastic splitting δ≳506–566 keV, which for a 248 keV xenon recoil demands lab-frame speeds v_min∼950–1025 km/s. In the SHM, the δ≳566 keV bound requires v_0≳240 km/s independent of v_esc — well beyond the 2σ range of any measured v_0 (up to 256 km/s), even at optimistic ρ_χ=0.45 GeV cm⁻³ and with a 5%-probability upward fluctuation. In the LMC-aware simulated halo, δ=514 keV is the largest splitting that yields one event in the 200–300 keV window; all curves fall below the fluctuation threshold by δ∼530 keV.

Why it matters: This is exactly the discriminator mode the digest tracks — an attempt to close the last astrophysical escape hatch rather than add another fit. The thermal higgsino is now doubly cornered: kinematics and solar capture together leave no viable window at δ≳566 keV.

Caveat: Only the weaker δ≳506 keV bound (tree-level Z up-scatter, not the loop-induced elastic channel) leaves a sliver of SHM viability, and only when both v_0 and v_esc sit at their upper limits. The LMC-tail extension beyond 950 km/s is a phenomenological exponential, not a simulated result.

arXiv:2609.15782 — Argon as the test of two interpretations of the LZ 248 keV recoil (Howard Baer et al.)

Baer and Barger reduce the endothermic-vs-exothermic debate to a single already-recorded measurement. Both interpretations require an internal splitting, but they flow energy oppositely. Read exothermically (pseudo-Dirac downscatter releasing |δ|), the event predicts a nuclear-recoil line in argon at E_Ar=|δ| m_χ/(m_χ+m_Ar) — 336 keV for m_χ=200 GeV, ranging 268–525 keV over the exothermic family — at ~3–4 events/tonne-yr, roughly ten times the equivalent xenon rate. Argon wins because its Helm form factor at 336 keV sits in the first diffraction lobe (F²⁼⁰.056) while xenon at 248 keV sits near its second-lobe minimum (F²⁼¹.6×10⁻⁴); the factorized rate ratio returns 9.5 at 200 GeV. Read endothermically (ground-state upscatter by the fast halo tail), argon predicts zero events: the argon threshold speed exceeds the halo maximum (1224 vs 796 km/s at 1.1 TeV). The ratio depends only on two-body kinematics, the two form factors, and the coupling’s charge structure — not the mediator or excited fraction.

Why it matters: DEAP-3600 already holds the data. The published 231-day exposure implies ~7 events (full target) or 1.7 (fiducial) at the benchmark rate; the 813-day first run holds ~25 and 6. A reanalysis for single-scatter nuclear recoils between 200–600 keV (near 85 keV_ee) either finds the line and fixes m_χ from the two line positions, or kills the exothermic reading — no new detector required.

Caveat: The fiducial mass at ~500 photoelectrons is unpublished; expected counts within the WIMP-search fiducial volume are only a few, and background control (shadowed alphas, ³⁹Ar, radiogenic neutrons) rests on DEAP’s own estimates.

arXiv:2609.15655 — First Observation of D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ (BESIII Collaboration et al.)

BESIII observes the semi-muonic decay D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ (with f_0→π⁺π⁻) for the first time, using 7.33 fb⁻¹ at E_CM=4.128–4.226 GeV and a double-tag technique (839k single tags across 15 hadronic modes). From 196±22 signal events they measure ℬ=(1.59±0.18_stat±0.11_syst)×10⁻³. Combined with the earlier BESIII electronic-channel result, the LFU ratio ℬ(μ)/ℬ(e)=0.92±0.13_stat±0.08_syst agrees with the SM range 0.94–1.11 — no LFU violation at current precision, and the first such test in a scalar-meson c→s transition. A dynamical fit (simple-pole form factor, relativistic Flatté line shape) yields f_+^f_0(0)|V_cs|=0.490±0.059±0.025; averaging with the electronic channel gives 0.500±0.016±0.020, and with CKMfitter |V_cs| the most precise D_s→f_0 form factor to date, f_+^f_0(0)=0.514±0.017±0.021.

Why it matters: Beyond extending LFU tests into scalar final states, the branching fraction implies a mixing angle ϕ=(28.0±26.6)^∘, favoring an ss̅-dominant f_0(980) in the qq̅ picture. The precise form factor discriminates sharply among models: consistent with CLFD/DR/QCDSR but in up-to-5σ tension with LCSR, LFQM, and CCQM predictions, all of which now incorporate the finite f_0 width. This is the consolidating-null flavor picture the digest notes — LFU intact, precision turned onto hadronic structure.

Caveat: The 13% statistical LFU uncertainty leaves ample room; the extracted ϕ carries a large error. μ/π misidentification is handled by retaining both track pairings and fitting the wrong-combination shape.

item.title: Monday, September 14, 2026
item.description:
The higgsino, from halo back to Run 2

For three weeks the higgsino has been a xenon story — one 248 keV recoil, fit and refit. Today Athron et al. arXiv:2609.12914 put it back where it is actually constrained: a global fit over 34 Run 2 LHC searches and 63 measurements. LZ traffic has meanwhile thinned to a handful of model-building follow-ups, and the day’s real breadth sits elsewhere — a gravitational-wave phase-transition cluster, a strong pair of haloscope results, and a genuine CMS light-pseudoscalar search. The month-long recoil spectacle is losing its grip on the front page.

Themes

The LZ event thins to model-building

Three follow-ups arrived, all trying to keep inelastic DM viable against the solar-capture bound. Okada et al. arXiv:2609.13038 use a scotogenic U(1)_X with isospin violation to suppress solar capture while keeping the xenon signal; Cabo-Almeida et al. arXiv:2609.13130 break the mass–cross-section relation with low-reheating freeze-in. Lee et al. arXiv:2609.12045 stand out for a genuinely different mechanism — invisible neutron-pair annihilation into a baryon-number-2 scalar, giving a monochromatic recoil with a common reconstructed mass across isotopes. The escape-hatch pattern continues, but the volume has dropped sharply from last week.

Electroweakinos, confronted with the LHC

Athron et al. arXiv:2609.12914 deliver the most complete collider summary of the MSSM electroweakino sector to date: for a light bino, m_χ̃_2⁰≳760 GeV; adding a light gravitino pushes exclusions toward 1 TeV, though a Higgsino-dominated χ̃_1⁰ needs only ~650 GeV. Individual ATLAS/CMS compressed-spectrum excesses can each be fit, but not simultaneously. This is the empirical backdrop the LZ-higgsino fits have mostly been ignoring.

Gravitational waves as a dark-sector ledger

A real cluster. Puchades-Ibáñez et al. arXiv:2609.12098 compute NLO nucleation for a supercooled transition and find it shifts the PTA-inferred gauge coupling by 9–13% — a concrete warning about first-order-PT interpretations of NANOGrav. An et al. arXiv:2609.12867 use LVK O1–O4a to constrain inflationary PBH mechanisms via scalar-induced GWs, already beating conventional abundance bounds. Alongside: Khalaf et al. arXiv:2609.12052 probe ultralight scalars through superradiance in LVK low-mass-ratio mergers, and Betancourt Kamenetskaia et al. arXiv:2609.12806 reconstruct a DM equation of state from inspiral dynamical friction. Ghosh’s GW atlas arXiv:2609.12664 is explicitly phenomenological.

Haloscopes and axion flavor

The axion detection wing from last week keeps producing. The DALI collaboration posts both a dark-photon exclusion — χ≲6.8×10⁻¹⁴ near 28.5 μeV, the strongest lab bound in that band arXiv:2609.12775 — and the resonator architecture behind it arXiv:2609.12776. On the model side, Cox et al. arXiv:2609.12635 build minimal flavoured DFSZ axions with unit domain-wall number, reconstructing the full quark Yukawa sector from measured masses and CKM.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.12914 — the definitive Run 2 collider picture of MSSM electroweakinos; the data-driven counterweight to a month of LZ higgsino fits.
  • arXiv:2609.12683 — CMS H→aa→μμττ, with boosted-ditau reconstruction and the first LHC ττ limits for a scalar up to 1 TeV.
  • arXiv:2609.12775 — DALI’s dark-photon result: strongest laboratory exclusion in its frequency band, from 36 hours of data.
  • arXiv:2609.12024 — Hay et al.’s metric-aware Deep Sets EMD surrogate: architectural constraints slash triangle-inequality violations without being told to.
  • arXiv:2609.12045 — invisible neutron-pair annihilation as an LZ reading, with a clean multi-isotope mass-reconstruction test.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.12928 NNLL resummation for four-top production — van Beekveld et al. (hep-ph) — threshold resummation matched to NLO for one of the rarest SM processes.
  • arXiv:2609.12800 Associated W+charm production — Alanko et al. (hep-ph) — ATLAS data favor zero strangeness asymmetry over MSHT20/NNPDF4.0.
  • arXiv:2609.12610 ResoSeg — Li et al. (hep-ex) — segmentation for resonance tagging at BESIII, doubling combined efficiency over the 16-channel approach.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.12914 — What has the LHC told us about the electroweakino sector of the MSSM? (Peter Athron et al.)

GAMBIT’s most complete collider recast of the MSSM electroweak sector to date: a frequentist global fit over 34 Run 2 LHC searches, 63 Run 2 measurements (via Contur), and LEP cross-section limits, scanning M_1, M_2, μ, tanβ with all other sparticles decoupled. The headline is that a genuine general bound now exists where the 2018 fit found none — for a light bino χ̃_1⁰, exclusion reaches m_χ̃_2⁰≳760 GeV in both the (m_χ̃_2⁰,m_χ̃_1⁰⁾ and chargino planes. Adding a light (m_3/2=1 eV) gravitino pushes exclusions to (m_χ̃_1⁰,m_χ̃_2⁰⁾∼(900,1000) GeV, but a Higgsino-dominated LSP survives down to ≈650 GeV. The much-discussed ATLAS soft-dilepton excess (Δm∼20 GeV) is reproduced as a weak preference near m_χ̃_2⁰≈200 GeV, but the CMS zero-lepton and soft-lepton searches disfavour exactly the ATLAS-preferred region — no scenario fits both simultaneously.

Why it matters: this is the empirical backdrop the month of LZ-higgsino fits has largely ignored. The Higgsino-degenerate corner that survives at ~650 GeV is precisely where compressed dark-matter scenarios live, and closing it at small Δm is conceded to be “very challenging” even at HL-LHC. Honest caveats: signal yields use LO+LL (not NLO) cross-sections, monojet and long-lived-particle searches are omitted, the b-jet regions of ATLAS_2BoostedBosons are not implemented, and the G̃-EWMSSM best fit rests on a 36 fb⁻¹ CMS diphoton excess that newer full-Run-2 photon searches do not corroborate.

arXiv:2609.12683 — Search for a light pseudoscalar Higgs boson in boosted μμττ final states (CMS Collaboration)

CMS searches H→aa→μμττ in 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data, where the large m_H–m_a hierarchy collimates each ττ pair. The key methodological advance is dedicated boosted-ditau reconstruction: modified HPS seeding for τ_μτ_h/τ_eτ_h (efficiency gains up to factors of 2–4 at high m_H), plus a new deep-network tagger, DeepDiTau, that classifies AK4 jets as τ_hτ_h at 70% efficiency and ~1% mistag — enabling the high-rate all-hadronic channel for the first time. Combining four ττ channels covers 94% of a→ττ decays. No excess is seen. Model-independent 95% CL limits on σ_H×ℬ/σ_SM reach 5×10⁻⁵ to 2.7×10⁻⁴ for m_a=3.6–21 GeV at m_H=125 GeV, and — for the first time at the LHC in ττ final states — extend to a heavy scalar up to m_H=1 TeV, where limits span 3.5×10⁻⁴ to 1.5×10⁻³ for m_a=3.6–50 GeV.

Why it matters: this is the day’s genuine light-pseudoscalar collider result, complementary to the LZ/axion model-building. It sets the most stringent ℬ(H→aa) limits to date for 3.6<m_a<4.2 GeV in Type-I/II 2HDM+S, improves on prior μμττ results by factors 2–5, and opens the heavy-scalar →aa window entirely. Caveats: sensitivity degrades at low m_a where decay products fully merge, Υ resonances contaminate near m_a≈10 GeV, and above 4.2 GeV the charm-tagging analysis remains stronger.

arXiv:2609.12775 — Constraints on Galactic Dark Photons from a DALI Prototype (Javier De Miguel et al.)

A proof-of-principle DALI haloscope — a 20-plate yttria-stabilized zirconia Fabry–Pérot resonator read out by an antenna, run at fixed λ/8 spacing with Q_L≈2200 near 6.907 GHz and T_sys≃59 K — reinterprets 36 hours of data (originally an axion search) as a dark-photon search. No magnetic field is needed since kinetic mixing converts dark photons at the dielectric discontinuities. After baseline removal, iterative RFI masking, grand-spectrum stacking with the lab-frame line shape, and an end-to-end injection efficiency of η_e2e≃0.60, no significant excess survives. Fourteen retained clusters all fall below adopted confidence and are flagged for rescan. The result excludes kinetic mixing χ≲6.8×10⁻¹⁴ at 28.54 μeV (6.902 GHz), across 88.1% of the unmasked 28.482–28.610 μeV band at 90% CL — claimed as the strongest laboratory bound in this frequency range.

Why it matters: it fits today’s haloscope theme (alongside DALI’s companion resonator paper), demonstrating that the open Fabry–Pérot architecture — whose cross section decouples from resonance frequency — can deliver competitive high-frequency limits with mature commercial hardware. As a magnet-free dark-photon channel, it is a cheap, fast complement to cavity haloscopes. Caveats are explicit: only a single frequency step (one plate spacing), a scaled-down prototype (~1:100 in area), an undercoupled antenna (β≃0.36), assumption that dark photons saturate the local density with randomly-oriented polarization (κ²⁼¹/3), and a residual 0.09σ baseline systematic.

item.title: Friday, September 11, 2026
item.description:
The LZ event looks for exits

Yesterday Langhoff exiled the thermal higgsino to 10⁵–10⁶ GeV; today the model-builders push back, trying to keep inelastic DM at ordinary scales by dodging the solar-capture bound rather than surrendering to it. Seven of the day’s papers touch the 248 keV recoil, and the useful ones are no longer fits but evasion strategies — light mediators, cosmic-ray boosting, two-component spectra. Meanwhile Nguyen et al. arXiv:2609.11833 reconfirm the Pospelov–Ramani bound in full generality, so the escape hatches have to work hard. Away from xenon, an axion-cosmology cluster and a clutch of collider spin/EFT papers carry the real methodological weight.

Themes

LZ: escape routes and a reconfirmed bound

The pattern is now evasion. Qi et al. arXiv:2609.10636 build a U(1)_B-3L_τ scalar whose f_n/f_p suppresses solar iron capture, arguing the electroweak solar bound doesn’t transfer to light-mediator realizations; Heikinheimo et al. arXiv:2609.11600 drop the halo tail entirely with cosmic-ray-boosted DM and momentum-dependent operators peaking at 248 keV; Fan et al. arXiv:2609.10491 use two-component exothermic scattering to cut the required cross section and relax IceCube. Frolovsky et al. arXiv:2609.11241 tie a 1 TeV higgsino to Starobinsky supergravity, and Li et al. arXiv:2609.10662 chase inelastic capture in primordial dark stars. Against all this, Nguyen et al. arXiv:2609.11833 confirm Pospelov and show the solar-neutrino non-excess constrains the whole inelastic class — the counter-pressure the memory has tracked for two weeks, now generalized.

An axion-cosmology cluster

A genuinely broad axion day, none of it about the LZ event. Luu et al. post a companion pair arXiv:2609.11055, arXiv:2609.11056 reconstructing the relativistic oscillations of cosmological axions in an EFT wavefunction picture — sub-percent accuracy, built for Boltzmann solvers. Gemmell et al. arXiv:2609.10674 resolve the order-of-magnitude disagreement in JWST decaying-axion limits, excluding QCD axion DM from 0.5–2.5 eV. Hook et al. arXiv:2609.10671 open axial-vector (Kalb–Ramond) ultralight DM, and Thongyoi et al. arXiv:2609.11254 relocate the SIMP miracle into an axion portal. The strong-CP/axion thread running since August keeps widening past the lattice program into cosmology and detection.

Collider spin, QI, and EFT

Kanachova et al. arXiv:2609.11151 extend collider quantum tomography to qubit-qutrit (Λϕ, ΛK^*0) systems, deriving entanglement certification from the incomplete 6×6 density matrix — the QI program reaching unequal-spin hadronic final states. Bellagroudi et al. arXiv:2609.11641 use top-spin correlations to separate a CP-odd 2HDM pseudoscalar from a leptophobic Z’ in tt̅ — directly relevant to the unresolved toponium-vs-scalar question. On the EFT side, Maskos et al. arXiv:2609.11681 deliver NLO SMEFT h→bb̅ in Sherpa, and Kala et al. arXiv:2609.11914 build the full RG framework for Dirac-fermion DMEFT.

QCD structure and lattice

Guyton et al. arXiv:2609.11026 give a full RBC/UKQCD determination of heavy-strange meson decay constants and compositeness, with first lattice results for f_B^*_s0 and f_B_s1 and evidence that the positive-parity states are predominantly molecular. Casalderrey-Solana et al. arXiv:2609.10679 present an “Efficient Wake” procedure for jet-medium response — tens of thousands of times faster than full hydro, aimed at Monte Carlo jet analyses.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.11151 — Kanachova et al. push collider quantum tomography to qubit-qutrit systems; a new probe of QCD hadronization from entangled quark pairs.
  • arXiv:2609.11026 — Guyton et al.’s heavy-strange meson lattice results, with first-ever f_B^*_s0, f_B_s1 and a molecular verdict on the positive-parity states.
  • arXiv:2609.11641 — Bellagroudi et al. turn top-spin correlations into a pseudoscalar-vs-vector discriminant — the toponium interpretation debate made quantitative.
  • arXiv:2609.10679 — Casalderrey-Solana et al.’s Efficient Wake: full-hydro-quality jet-wake distributions at 10⁴× the speed, ready to drop into Hybrid-Model MC.
  • arXiv:2609.11833 — Nguyen et al. generalize the solar-neutrino bound across the whole inelastic-DM class favored by LZ; the day’s firmest constraint.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.11461 Combinations… using the BLUE method — Dado et al. (physics.data-an) — BLUE extended to fit nuisance parameters jointly, flagging Convino’s underestimated uncertainties.
  • arXiv:2609.10891 Mitigating Sensor Cracking… ATLAS ITk Strip — ATLAS ITk Strips Collaboration (physics.ins-det) — the interposer strategy adopted for the barrel after zero fractures in testing.
  • arXiv:2609.10681 Opening the Topological Portal to Dark Sectors — Davighi et al. (hep-ph) — a weakly-coupled UV completion of the QCD-to-dark-pion topological portal, testable at FCC-ee.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.11151 — Qubit-Qutrit Quantum Tomography of hadronic Λφ and ΛK*⁰ systems (Veronica Kanachova et al.)

Extending collider quantum tomography to unequal-spin final states, Kanachova et al. formalize the spin-½⊗1 density matrix for Λφ and ΛK*⁰ pairs and confront its inescapable incompleteness: the parity-violating Λ→pπ⁻ is fully self-analyzing, but the parity-conserving V→PP decay carries no rank-1 (dipole) analyzer, so only 23 of the 35 spin parameters are measurable — the meson vector polarization Pᵢ (3) and the dipole–dipole correlations Cᵢⱼ (9) drop out identically. The key result is that entanglement can still be certified exactly from this censored data. Zeroing the 12 missing parameters is equivalent to a “partial time reversal” on the meson (𝒰_B∘T_B), and the reconstruction ρ_meas satisfies ρ_meas^{T_B}=𝒰_B(ρ_meas), so the Peres–Horodecki test collapses to a single diagonalization: a negative eigenvalue of ρ_meas certifies entanglement, with no false positives, and no analysis of the same 23 observables can do better. Pure entangled states retain exactly half their negativity; mixed states have quantifiable “blind windows” (e.g. isotropic-noise dilution entangled for p>1/4 but uncertifiable until p>2/5).

Why it matters: this opens a new hadronization probe. Because local dressing cannot create entanglement, surviving correlations lower-bound the quark-pair correlation at production, and comparing degradation in Λφ/ΛK*⁰ (meson channel) against ΛΛ̄ (baryon channel) as a function of ΔR isolates p_meson vs p_baryon — a coherence-transport quantity never measured. Estimators are simple angular moments extractable from existing datasets. Caveat: the theorems’ validity relies on the specific 12-parameter censoring; other 12-subsets give false positives, and much of the numerical verification was AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5) with a stated but unproven pure-state conjecture.

arXiv:2609.11026 — Positive- and negative-parity charm-strange and bottom-strange mesons from lattice QCD (Forrest Guyton et al.)

Guyton and Meinel deliver a full RBC/UKQCD determination of decay constants, binding energies, and Weinberg compositeness for the lightest scalar, pseudoscalar, vector, and axial-vector Dₛ and Bₛ mesons, using domain-wall light/strange quarks and anisotropic clover charm/bottom on seven ensembles (mπ = 139–431 MeV, a = 0.073–0.114 fm) with combined chiral-continuum extrapolation. For negative-parity states they obtain f_{Dₛ}=251.4(2.1)(0.4)(2.5) MeV, f_{Dₛ*}=272.5(4.3)(1.0)(2.7), f_{Bₛ}=228.4(5.8)(0.5)(2.3), f_{Bₛ*}=229.2(4.4)(0.8)(2.3) MeV, plus ratios f_{Dₛ*}/f_{Dₛ}=1.086(14)(11) and f_{Bₛ*}/f_{Bₛ}=1.003(22)(10), consistent with FLAG. The positive-parity sector uses a GEVP with q̄q, derivative, and meson-meson-scattering operators (the latter at both source and sink), Lüscher’s method, and effective-range expansions to extract infinite-volume bound-state masses: m_{Dₛ0*}−m_D−m_K=−48(14)(4) MeV, m_{Dₛ1}−m_{D*}−m_K=−61(15)(2), m_{Bₛ0*}−m_B−m_K=−69(13)(4), m_{Bₛ1}−m_{B*}−m_K=−77(10)(5). The charm results agree with experiment (−45.0(6), −44.7(6) MeV). Positive-parity decay constants — including the first-ever lattice f_{Bₛ0*}=207(12)(8)(2) and f_{Bₛ1}=196(16)(11)(2) MeV — are reported.

Why it matters: the below-threshold binding, small positive-parity decay constants, and scattering lengths consistently support a predominantly D⁽⁾K/B⁽⁾K molecular interpretation of the Dₛ0*(2317)-like states, and the negative-parity constants feed dispersive bounds on b→s form factors relevant to the b→sℓℓ anomalies. Caveats acknowledged: two-pion left-hand cuts (which extend above the ground-state energies at low mπ) are neglected, invalidating strict Lüscher/ERE there, and weak-binding corrections to Weinberg’s criterion are expected to be large in some channels.

arXiv:2609.11641 — Distinguishing a pseudoscalar from a vector t t̄ resonance with top-quark spin correlations at the HL-LHC (Ahmed Bellagroudi et al.)

Bellagroudi and Fassi ask a post-discovery question: given a t t̄ resonance, can dilepton spin correlations separate a CP-odd 2HDM pseudoscalar A (0⁻, spin-singlet ¹S₀, iγ₅ vertex) from a leptophobic topcolor Z′ (1⁻, chiral vector)? Using MadGraph+Pythia+Delphes with matrix-element spin-preserving decays and neutrino-weighting reconstruction, they find a parton-level helicity-correlation gap Δc_hel≃0.43 (A: +0.33, Z′: −0.08), nearly mass-independent, surviving reconstruction with dilution ≈0.66. Normalizing A to CMS HIG-22-013 coupling limits and rate-matching Z′ so the test probes spin structure, the LO t t̄-only baseline gives 2.27σ (400 GeV) and 2.74σ (800 GeV) at 3000 fb⁻¹, using a 4×4 (c_hel, c_han) template likelihood. Reverse non-nested direction agrees; equal-yield tests give 1.86 and 2.70σ (confirming 800 GeV is shape-driven); profiling a Gaussian-constrained SM c_hel nuisance yields 2.07/2.63σ (optimistic) down to 1.67/2.26σ. A g⁴-mapped scan places 5σ at couplings ~22%/16% above reference.

Why it matters: this makes the toponium-vs-scalar interpretation debate quantitative, showing spin correlations can in principle assign resonance spin/parity where a rate excess cannot. The 800 GeV point is the cleanest demonstration; 400 GeV is intrinsically fragile because the near-threshold SM continuum is itself spin-singlet/pseudoscalar-like (the same physics driving threshold entanglement enhancement), and 1500 GeV is unreachable (~12 events). Honest caveats abound: LO normalization, fixed on-shell widths, no non-t t̄ backgrounds, and — critically — omitted signal–continuum interference, plus a single-mode “bracket” nuisance rather than a proper mass-dependent sideband fit.

Citation radar

This week’s radar is a single-topic feeding frenzy. Every paper below was posted within days of the LUX-ZEPLIN Collaboration’s late-August preprint reporting one nuclear-recoil-like event at E_R = 248±23±23 keV in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure (3.4σ local, 2.6σ global). The community has converged with remarkable speed on a single reading — endothermic/inelastic dark matter, whose threshold kinematics naturally selects a high, localized recoil energy that conventional elastic WIMP spectra cannot reproduce — and is now racing to claim the most predictive particle realization. The result is a tight cluster of cross-citing papers (they reference each other heavily), which explains the near-identical citation counts. This is what a fresh anomaly looks like when it hits a theory community primed with a ready-made mechanism.

arXiv:2609.02608 — Dark Matter at the Kinematic Edge: Interpreting the 248 keV LZ Nuclear-Recoil Candidate (Mattia Di Mauro)

Di Mauro provides the most thorough single-author phenomenological recast of the LZ event. Using the published efficiency curves and operator significances, the paper argues that elastic spin-independent scattering fails quantitatively — normalizing to one event near 248 keV would demand ~1.4×10³ accompanying low-energy recoils — while endothermic inelastic scattering shifts the spectrum into the observed window. Two concrete realizations are worked out: a thermal pseudo-Dirac fermion with off-diagonal vector coupling (m_χ≃1 TeV, δ≃297 keV, σ_N≃6.5×10⁻⁴³ cm²) that ties the direct-detection rate to relic-abundance coannihilation, and a more predictive thermal Higgsino (1.1 TeV, δ≃377 keV) testable via a gamma-ray line.

At ~41 citations in roughly a month, this reads as the community’s reference recast: it carefully catalogs which NREFT operators LZ actually tested, stresses that the event selects “spectral hardness” rather than a unique Lorentz structure, and quantifies halo-tail sensitivity. Its detailed efficiency digitization and explicit relic–direct-detection relation make it a natural citation anchor for the follow-up papers below.

arXiv:2609.01475 — Inelastic Dark Matter Signature at High Recoil Energy in LUX-ZEPLIN and CRESST (Liangliang Su et al.)

Su, Yang, and Yang deliver a compact Letter interpreting the event as endothermic inelastic DM, adding a distinctive ingredient: terrestrial propagation. They compute both direct scattering of surviving ground-state halo DM and the excited-state component produced by upscattering inside the Earth, concluding that for m_χ≳500 GeV and δ=𝒪(300) keV the Earth-produced component is kinematically forbidden — leaving direct endothermic scattering on xenon as the signal and eliminating daily modulation. An illustrative two-bin likelihood gives a best-fit (m_χ,δ)≃(1.105 TeV,350 keV) for σ̅_n=10⁻³⁷ cm².

The headline forward-looking claim — testability via the planned CRESST upgrade, whose heavier tungsten target reaches the same transition at lower recoil energy with ~1.5 tonne·day exposure — gives experimentalists a concrete target and likely drives some of its ~41 citations. As one of the earliest posted (Sept 1) interpretations, it also functions as a template others cite when framing the inelastic reading and the CRESST complementarity.

arXiv:2609.02807 — A Peccei-Quinn Origin for Inelastic Electroweak Dark Matter after LUX-ZEPLIN (Luca Visinelli)

Visinelli embeds the inelastic electroweak-doublet interpretation in a Peccei–Quinn completion: spontaneous PQ breaking leaves a residual parity that stabilizes the lighter neutral state and generates the Majorana splitting via a heavy PQ-charged singlet, while a KSVZ colored pair supplies the QCD anomaly. Integrating out the singlet yields the dimension-five operator that splits a vectorlike doublet, giving a Higgsino-like off-diagonal Z coupling. The construction realizes a mixed axion–WIMP cosmology: for benchmark doublet masses 287–509 GeV the EW component supplies only 7–21% of the relic density, with the QCD axion providing the rest through misalignment (v_S≃4.4×10¹¹ GeV).

The paper is notable for its careful complementarity discussion — solar-capture/IceCube limits, excited-state radiative decay (~20 km decay length, leaving LZ a clean single recoil but enabling luminous scintillator signatures), and collider disappearing-track bounds. Its ~39 citations likely reflect both the appeal of unifying the two leading DM paradigms and its extensive, honest cross-referencing of the competing LZ interpretations, which positions it centrally in the emerging literature web.

arXiv:2609.02868 — Inelastic Dark Photon Dark Matter for the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event and the Galactic Halo Gamma-Ray Excess (Kimiko Yamashita)

Yamashita attempts a two-anomaly fit: a U(1)_X dark-photon DM at m_X=420 GeV that both explains Totani’s halo-like Fermi-LAT gamma-ray excess (via a p-wave-suppressed, Sommerfeld-enhanced W⁺W⁻ channel) and the LZ event (via inelastic X+N→V+N with δ≃316 keV, saturating the kinematic ceiling for xenon). A second light scalar ϕ’ mediates the inelastic transition while a dark parity forbids the elastic amplitude that would otherwise violate SI limits.

The ambition — one dark sector, two independent anomalies, same 420 GeV mass — is the clear draw, and at ~35 citations it is well-cited despite requiring a fairly elaborate scalar sector (the paper candidly defers “a full symmetry construction” and a profile-likelihood significance to future work). It leans on the same detector-resolution smearing (σ_E=32.5 keV) argument as the others. The transparent AI-assistance disclosure is a sign of the times. Its citation count is somewhat inflated by membership in the tightly cross-citing LZ cluster.

arXiv:2609.01892 — A PQ-Symmetric High-Scale SUSY Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil (Wen Yin)

Yin reads the event as near-threshold upscattering of 1.08-TeV thermal Higgsino dark matter, with a neutral-Higgsino splitting of 0.28–0.35 MeV fixing electroweak gauginos at 𝒪(10⁷⁾ GeV via the standard integrating-out relation δ_0≃m_Z²⁽s_W²/M_1+c_W²/M_2). The paper then builds out the full high-scale SUSY picture: gravity-mediated sfermions at ∼10⁷ GeV, a Kim–Nilles PQ mechanism setting μ=1.08 TeV plus a QCD axion, HSSUSY-checked Higgs mass at tanβ≃1.9–2.2, gauge unification with suppressed proton decay, and avoidance of the gravitino/moduli problems.

The distinctive prediction — a “super-invisible” axion with accidentally cancelled photon coupling (E/N=2 from the Higgsino contribution) — plus potential proton-decay reach make this a smoking-gun-oriented scenario. At ~32 citations it is the most model-building-heavy entry, cited as the SUSY-embedded counterpart to the more agnostic Higgsino recasts. The framing throughout is appropriately cautious, treating the single non-blind event as a “working hypothesis.”

item.title: Thursday, September 10, 2026
item.description:
The higgsino gets exiled to 10⁵ TeV

Four weeks on, the LZ recoil still anchors the day, but the interpretation has run out of ordinary places to hide. Langhoff arXiv:2609.09385 takes the thermal-higgsino reading to its conclusion: the empty sideband plus IceCube solar capture force the mass to 10⁵–10⁶ GeV, which cannot come from standard freeze-out — so it is produced during early matter domination via a Kim-Nilles mechanism that also solves strong CP. Meanwhile Chattaraj et al. arXiv:2609.10504 close off the mundane alternative, ruling out coherent neutrino scattering (SM, BSM, and exotic fluxes) as the source. The model zoo the memory has tracked since late August is now visibly straining against its own bounds.

Themes

The LZ event — exclusions and exotic escapes

The pivot from fits to constraints continues. Khan et al. arXiv:2609.09230 ask whether a resolved nuclear cancellation in elastic scattering can fake the 248 keV feature, and propose an argon target-scaling test to distinguish it from dark-sector excitation. He arXiv:2609.10453 and Fan et al. arXiv:2609.10491 push the transition-dipole and two-component exothermic readings that dodge the halo tail, while Chatterjee et al. arXiv:2609.09830 redo the radiative corrections to the higgsino splitting. Langhoff’s arXiv:2609.09385 and Chattaraj’s arXiv:2609.10504 are the ones that move the needle.

Axions and low-background instruments

A quietly strong instrumentation day. Kim et al. arXiv:2609.09717 report a TM₀₂₀ higher-order-mode haloscope with auxetic tuning that beats the usual volume penalty at high mass — ~300 MHz of contiguous KSVZ-approaching coverage, the live axion wing from last week extending upward. Alongside: McKie et al.’s arXiv:2609.09843 negative-ion TPC running on plain CF₄ (directional-DM relevant), KAPAE Phase II underground arXiv:2609.10259, and PandaX’s most stringent 0ν4β limit on ¹³⁶Xe arXiv:2609.10048 — a Dirac-neutrino probe.

Hadron structure and heavy-flavor

Ji et al. arXiv:2609.09318 combine near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction with quark-sector data to extract the nucleon’s strong-interaction size, 0.94±0.09 fm — larger than both charge and mass radii. On the flavor side, Ni et al. arXiv:2609.09802 flag a persistent Ξ_c⁰→Ξ⁻e⁺ν discrepancy (theory/lattice ~4% vs the experimental average), and Barger arXiv:2609.09262 offers a parameter-free level-four modular-symmetry fit to the full quark/lepton spectrum — the year’s flavor-numerology spine still alive.

ML and quantum tooling

The autodiff/ML wave keeps spreading. Stamenkovic et al. arXiv:2609.09275 bring self-supervised transformers to LHCb heavy-flavor tagging, learning decay maps from data without labels — a genuinely different tagging paradigm for the experiment. Kumar et al. arXiv:2609.10382 apply reinforcement learning to search SMEFT operator space for anomaly explanations, and Shu et al. arXiv:2609.10383 quantify JUNO’s oscillation-parameter reach via quantum Fisher information.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.09385 — Langhoff: the higgsino reading survives only at 10⁵–10⁶ GeV via early matter domination, tying the LZ event to strong CP.
  • arXiv:2609.09318 — Ji et al.’s nucleon strong-interaction radius from charmonium photoproduction; a clean, quotable number.
  • arXiv:2609.10504 — Chattaraj et al. rule out every neutrino-scattering explanation of LZ230616; the useful null of the day.
  • arXiv:2609.09717 — Kim et al.’s higher-order-mode haloscope beats the TM₀₁₀ volume penalty; a real high-mass axion limit.
  • arXiv:2609.09275 — Self-supervised transformer tagging for LHCb, extending reach to decays with invisible final states.

From the community

Larkoski’s arXiv:2609.09785 More QCD Masterclass Lectures on Jet Physics and Machine Learning — Larkoski (hep-ph) adds anomaly detection, scaling laws, and classification limits to the 2024 notes, deriving ML results from QCD first principles — and opens “with an apology for humanist physics.”

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.10288 Operation and performance of PLUME at LHCb — Alessio et al. (hep-ex) — bunch-by-bunch luminosity monitoring across Run 3.
  • arXiv:2609.10327 Towards new D meson fragmentation functions — Epele et al. (hep-ph) — the Hymn collaboration, separating prompt and non-prompt for the first time.
  • arXiv:2609.09276 Universal Entanglement Dynamics of Unitary Operators — Low et al. (quant-ph) — entangling-power stationary points as “corners,” feeding the collider-QI program.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.09385 — Heavy Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event (Kevin Langhoff)

Langhoff performs a 2D likelihood fit of pure-higgsino inelastic scattering to the LZ 248 keV recoil plus the empty high-energy sideband (350–675 keV), then folds in recomputed IceCube solar-capture bounds. The data alone prefer a light branch, m_χ≈(240,450) GeV, but that region is excluded by solar capture (which sets a floor on the splitting δ via neutrinos from captured-higgsino annihilation). The thermal higgsino at 1.1 TeV overfills the sideband (N_SB≳2, Δχ² up to 11). The only corner consistent with the event, the empty sideband and solar capture is m_χ≈(10⁵,10⁶⁾ GeV with δ≈(330,480) keV — where DM dilution (ρ∝1/m_χ) forces small δ and the sideband/ROI event ratio lands near 0.8–1 (versus ∼0.1 light, ≳15 thermal), a testable prediction. Such a heavy higgsino cannot arise from freeze-out, so he builds a proof-of-concept: freeze-out during early matter domination reheating to T_RH≈1 TeV, tied to the μ term via a Kim-Nilles mechanism that also solves strong CP.

Why it matters: it closes today’s headline arc — the ordinary thermal reading is dead, and survival demands a 10⁷ GeV gaugino scale plus a bespoke cosmology, connecting a direct-detection anomaly to axion/strong-CP physics. Caveats are frank: the Δχ² contours are a “heuristic guide” only, the heavy point is not the best fit, results depend on LMC-tail halo modeling, solar-capture curves bracket limiting behavior rather than a precise bound, and the model needs a tuned axion misalignment (θ≲0.05).

arXiv:2609.09318 — Nucleon Strong-Interaction Size from Charmonium Photoproduction (Xiangdong Ji et al.)

Ji, Joosten, Meziani, and Pefkou extract the nucleon’s overall strong-interaction radius by combining world near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction data (GlueX, Hall C, CLAS12) with a recent Bayesian quark-sector GFF analysis. Fitting the differential cross sections in a holographic-QCD model — A_g(t) dipole, C_g(t) tripole, B_g=0 — yields the gluon stress-energy form factors (χ²/ndf=1.005 after dropping the lowest GlueX energy bin). Energy-momentum conservation then relates the total A,C form factors to the scalar (trace-anomaly) color-field distribution G^s(t), whose Breit-frame radius is ⟨r_s²⟩¹/2=0.94±0.09 fm — larger than the PDG charge radius (0.8409 fm) and larger than the mass radius, defining a gluonic “skin” analogous to the neutron skin in ²⁰⁸Pb.

Why it matters: it delivers a clean, quotable first experimental number for the nucleon’s strong-interaction extent, mapping the color field that generates most of the nucleon mass rather than its charge. The ordering (strong > charge > mass) agrees with lattice and dispersive determinations cited. Caveats are stated plainly: the identification of the photoproduction amplitude with the gluonic SET is framework-dependent (open-charm and alternative production mechanisms may contaminate), B_g=0 is an assumption, and the result inherits both statistical and model uncertainty. SoLID and EIC/ePIC are projected to improve precision by up to an order of magnitude.

arXiv:2609.10504 — Can Elastic Neutrino Scattering Account for the LZ230616 Event? (Ayan Chattaraj et al.)

Chattaraj et al. systematically test whether coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering (CEνNS) can produce the 248 keV LZ recoil. Kinematics alone require E_ν≳118 MeV, killing solar and DSNB fluxes; only atmospheric neutrinos reach that energy, but their SM rate in the signal bin (225–271 keV) is R_I≃2×10⁻⁶ events. Introducing BSM scalar or vector mediators tuned to give one signal-region event overshoots the low-energy bins by 𝒪(10⁵⁾ events — six orders of magnitude above background — so the R_I=1 contour sits entirely inside the R_II-excluded region. Exotic monochromatic fluxes fare no better: DM annihilation (χχ→νν̅) requires ⟨σv⟩≳10⁻¹⁸ cm³/s and DM decay τ_χ≲10¹⁵ s, both far past existing bounds, while overpopulating low-recoil bins by hundreds of events. PBH evaporation is worst: the exponentially soft Hawking spectrum gives R_II/R_I∼10⁴–10²³ and demands f_PBH≳95, exceeding the total DM density.

Why it matters: the useful null of the day. The broad recoil spectrum inherent to elastic scattering is fundamentally incompatible with an isolated high-energy feature, reinforcing that the LZ event demands an inelastic/threshold mechanism (higgsino, exothermic DM). Caveat: the analysis is deliberately restricted to elastic channels — inelastic neutrino processes and atmospheric-neutrino upscattering (their ref. [29]) are outside scope.

item.title: Wednesday, September 9, 2026
item.description:
The LZ event turns testable

Week three of the LZ recoil, and roughly a quarter of today’s 127 papers are still interpreting one event. The model-building has saturated — inert doublets, singlet-doublets, B-L scalars, GUT embeddings, dark dimensions, warped extra dimensions all fit the same 248 keV — so the useful papers are no longer the fits but the tests. Two things changed the register today: the bounds keep arriving (Bose et al. arXiv:2609.07807 and Di Mauro et al. arXiv:2609.06760 both re-execute the solar-capture argument that killed the thermal Higgsino), and the interpretations are finally reaching out to colliders, argon, and directional signals. Away from xenon, the genuine physics is a jet-quenching color-decoherence pair and a clutch of real axion and neutrino results.

Themes

The LZ zoo, and the pivot to falsifiability

The endothermic Higgsino is now excluded from every direction — Bose et al. arXiv:2609.07807 push the Super-K/IceCube splitting bound to ≳557 keV, Di Mauro et al. arXiv:2609.06760 confirm the thermal Higgsino dies while generic endothermic survives. So the field is escaping in three directions: away from the halo tail via boosted dark matter (Kannike et al. arXiv:2609.07742, Alhazmi et al. arXiv:2609.06890, Liang et al. arXiv:2609.06756) and exothermic scattering (Baer et al. arXiv:2609.06153, with a clean argon prediction); toward exotic mechanisms like neutron disappearance (Aghaie et al. arXiv:2609.09037); and, most usefully, toward collider tests — Cheung et al. arXiv:2609.08712 predict sub-cm disappearing tracks from the Higgsino chargino, Kotlarski et al. arXiv:2609.06750 tie the splitting to a 10s-of-TeV Z’ at FCC-hh. Asadi et al. arXiv:2609.09107 stand out for a distinctive signature rather than another fit.

Jet quenching gets its colors

Bossi et al. arXiv:2609.05609 combine inclusive jet R_AA with energy-energy correlators to extract quark and gluon quenching factors, finding coherent energy loss incompatible with Casimir scaling — until color decoherence is added, which restores it. Mehtar-Tani arXiv:2609.05614 supplies the generating-functional machinery for exactly this coherent-to-incoherent EEC evolution. A clean data-plus-theory pairing, and a genuinely new thread against the LZ noise.

Axions, lab to starlight

Two real experimental limits landed: Lee et al. arXiv:2609.08144 reach 1.3×KSVZ at 15.6 μeV with a broadly tunable HTS cavity, and Winter et al. arXiv:2609.07908 bound the axion-EDM coupling via ²⁰⁷Pb solid-state NMR. Levasseur et al. arXiv:2609.08504 deliver a distance-independent RGB-star bound on the axion-electron coupling, and Witte et al. arXiv:2609.08840 work out axion-hair pulsar electrodynamics. The strong-CP thread the memory has tracked since August now has a live detection wing.

Neutrino experiments clear the ledger

NOvA’s dual-baseline sterile search arXiv:2609.08900 finds nothing and excludes most of IceCube’s allowed region — its first analysis to fit neutrino and antineutrino modes jointly. Alongside: NOvA’s neutron-response remodeling arXiv:2609.06956, and Lunardini et al.’s arXiv:2609.08753 two-parameter DSNB template as detectors approach discovery.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.08712 — Cheung et al. turn the LZ Higgsino into a disappearing-track prediction; the cleanest LZ-to-collider bridge today.
  • arXiv:2609.09107 — Asadi et al.’s magnetic inelastic dark baryons predict a coincident photon at energy δ — a directional-detection handle no other iDM reading offers.
  • arXiv:2609.05609 — Bossi et al.: EEC-plus-R_AA evidence that the QGP resolves jet substructure, restoring Casimir scaling through color decoherence.
  • arXiv:2609.08144 — Lee et al.’s HTS-cavity haloscope, KSVZ-level sensitivity at 15.6 μeV; a real axion limit, not a projection.
  • arXiv:2609.08900 — NOvA excludes sterile parameter space previously allowed by IceCube; a decisive null.

From the community

Mikhasenko et al. arXiv:2609.05719 AI in Particle Physics Education report a candid, mixed experience redesigning an intro course around AI-permitted, research-shaped assignments — engagement up, foundational objectives not reliably secured. And Knights et al. arXiv:2609.07523 Reducing simulation-related emissions in rare-event searches offer systematic guidance on event-biasing to cut the computing carbon footprint of background simulations.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.05829 CP Asymmetry Parameters and Polarization Correlations in Ω⁻Ω̄⁺ Pairs — BESIII (hep-ex) — first CP-sensitive φ_CP for the Ω, consistent with symmetry.
  • arXiv:2609.08392 Precision Higgs at a 10 TeV muon collider — Andreetto et al. (hep-ex) — 5% self-coupling from HH→bbbb; the self-coupling thread reaching the muon-collider case.
  • arXiv:2609.07467 Baryon number freeze-out in the Standard Model, precisely — Benso et al. (hep-ph) — sphaleron conversion factors nailed across the electroweak crossover.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.08712 — From LUX-ZEPLIN to Colliders: Probing Higgsino Dark Matter (Kingman Cheung et al.)

Taking the 248 keV LZ recoil at face value as 1.1 TeV thermal Higgsino inelastic DM with neutral splitting δm_0≃350 keV, Cheung, Kang, and Kumar work out the necessary collider corollary: the charged Higgsino sits Δm_+∼(330–350) MeV above the neutral state (electroweak loops dominating over a ∼-9 MeV finite-gaugino tree contribution), giving proper lifetime τ≈0.025 ns, cτ≃(6–8) mm, and decays to a soft ∼300 MeV pion. This is a sub-centimeter disappearing tracklet. Current ATLAS disappearing-track (m_χ^±≲225 GeV) and CMS soft-track (≲185 GeV) limits sit far below the 1.1 TeV target because the survival probability through three pixel hits (R∼9 cm) is ∼3×10⁻⁶ at β_Tγ=1; the 0.57 fb production cross section compounds the problem. HL-LHC needs better short-track reconstruction, not luminosity; dedicated studies find 5σ reach at a 100 TeV collider (30 ab⁻¹) and a 10 TeV muon collider (10 ab⁻¹).

Why it matters: this is the digest’s cleanest LZ-to-collider bridge, converting a direct-detection splitting into a one-parameter trajectory in the (m_χ^±,cτ) plane — a genuinely falsifiable prediction rather than another fit. Caveats are stated honestly: the authors flag the unresolved high-energy S1c sideband tension (acceptance not public), note the charged splitting is not a precision pole-mass calculation, and stress the collider reaches are conditional projections tied to assumed detector geometry and beam-induced backgrounds.

arXiv:2609.09107 — For Whom the Xenon Recoils: Magnetic Inelastic Dark Baryons (Pouya Asadi et al.)

Asadi et al. build a strongly-coupled dark-baryon model where a transition magnetic dipole operator (g_M≃-2√(3), roughly twice the neutron moment) drives inelastic scattering while an accidental “ℋ-parity” forbids all diagonal one-photon moments, suppressing elastic scattering. In the benchmark N_c=N_f=3 theory with dark quarks in an SU(2)_L triplet, the neutral 3-plet/5-plet baryons carry opposite ℋ-parity; hyperfine and W-exchange contributions to their splitting produce δ∼𝒪(100) keV near dark-quark mass ∼800 GeV (m_χ∼2.4 TeV). Fitting the LZ event (spin-dependent nuclear response) gives best-fit (m_χ,δ)=(6.8 TeV,300 keV) for SHM and (14 TeV,280 keV) for a MW+LMC profile, with viable ranges 1–50 TeV and 100–500 keV.

The distinctive handle: the excited state de-excites via a photon of energy δ, with decay length ∼4.7 m — comparable to detector size — so a fraction of recoils carry a coincident 100–500 keV photon, offering directional information (the excited state travels with the heavy DM), a discriminant no other iDM reading provides. It also predicts weaker solar-capture constraints (spin-dependent capture on rare odd-mass isotopes; annihilation dominantly to dark mesons rather than neutrinos), evading the bounds killing the thermal Higgsino. Caveats: mass-splitting predictions carry 𝒪(10⁷⁾ dynamic-range uncertainty from the variational quark-model estimate (only lattice could sharpen them), the single-event fit neglects backgrounds, and halo-profile choice dominates the preferred region.

arXiv:2609.05609 — The Colors of Jet Quenching (Hannah Bossi et al.)

Bossi, Larose, and Mehtar-Tani perform a data-driven extraction of quark and gluon quenching factors by jointly fitting ATLAS inclusive-jet R_AA and CMS energy-energy correlators (EECs) for R=0.4 jets, restricted to the small-angle region (R_L<0.07) where hard-collinear dynamics dominate and soft medium response is subleading. The two observables have complementary flavor sensitivity — gluon EECs peak at R_L=0.025 versus 0.012 for quarks — breaking the identifiability problem that plagues R_AA-only extractions. Under the coherent-energy-loss null hypothesis they extract S_q≃0.8, S_g≃0.3, incompatible with Casimir scaling (S_g=S_q⁹/4≃0.54–0.58) at 8–11σ. Adding color decoherence via the antenna/dipole quenching factor S_dip(θ) — which interpolates from coherent (θ≪θ_c) to independent loss with a slow θ⁻²/3 power-law tail — improves the fit (χ²/dof 0.93→0.13) and restores Casimir scaling (S_q≃0.65, S_g≃0.40, within 1.5σ). The medium resolution angle is tightly constrained: θ_c=0.057±0.005 (fit)⁺⁰.014_-0.008 (syst), p_T-independent as expected.

Why it matters: this is direct evidence, drawn from data rather than tuned Monte Carlo, that the QGP partially resolves internal jet substructure down to θ_c≃0.05–0.07 — the color-decoherence transition made quantitative, paired with Mehtar-Tani’s companion generating-functional derivation. Caveats are stated plainly: absolute χ² values are not meaningful because published uncertainties are added in quadrature without correlations, so only relative fit quality is claimed; it is a proof-of-concept, not a global analysis, with vacuum reference and flavor fractions held fixed and higher-order/medium-response effects deferred.

item.title: Monday, September 7, 2026
item.description:
The LZ event flips to exothermic

For a week the LZ recoil was read as an endothermic higgsino, and for a week that reading got shot down — Pospelov’s solar bound, Rodd’s empty sideband, McCabe’s runaway modulation. Today the interpretation switches sign: three papers move to exothermic inelastic dark matter, where the ambient state down-scatters and dumps its splitting as recoil, sidestepping the high-velocity-tail dependence that made the endothermic case fragile. Away from xenon, the day’s real breadth is a cluster of long-lived-particle proposals that repurpose existing detectors, plus two clean CMS measurements.

Themes

The LZ event turns exothermic

Dent et al. arXiv:2609.04673, de Lima arXiv:2609.05204, and Gu et al. arXiv:2609.05291 all pivot to exothermic scattering, which naturally produces a recoil peak at ~250 keV with no lower-energy activity and is “largely insensitive to halo uncertainties” — precisely the vulnerability that killed the endothermic reading. Dent uses the empty high-energy sideband to prefer sharper (lighter, larger-δ) peaks and predicts ~4.5 events in LZ’s 1000-day run; de Lima lands at m_χ∼30–200 GeV, δ∼0.5–1 MeV in a dark-photon model with testable argon/germanium signals; Gu works the inelastic-xenon excitation companion channel. The kinematics still fix the physics, but exothermic buys back the halo robustness the field spent last week losing.

Long-lived particles, borrowed detectors

Four papers turn detectors built for something else into LLP traps. Bolton et al. probe νSMEFT HNLs via displaced dilepton vertices at Belle II arXiv:2609.04332; Min et al. show LHC-produced long-lived particles decaying inside KM3NeT/ORCA could set among the strongest limits on kaon-to-LLP decays arXiv:2609.04386; and a second Bolton et al. paper reads displaced Majoron decays inside 0νββ experiments as a two-orders-of-magnitude sensitivity gain arXiv:2609.05352. The sharpest is Wang arXiv:2609.04761: under a shared-coupling condition the flavor ratio of displaced leptons is fixed by PMNS data alone, giving N_e/N_μ=0.14 (normal) vs 2.11 (inverted) — a δ_CP-free collider handle on mass ordering. This extends the GRENDEL-style repurposing thread from earlier in the week.

CMS: two clean measurements

CMS observes a negative azimuthal asymmetry A_2=-0.194 at >5σ for coherently photoproduced J/ψ in PbPb arXiv:2609.04376 — first direct evidence the meson inherits the incident photon’s linear polarization, and a possible new reaction-plane handle. Separately, the rare loop-induced H→Zγ decay comes in at μ=1.10⁺⁰.52_-0.61, 1.9σ observed arXiv:2609.04402 — SM-consistent, still statistics-limited.

Precision from EFT and lattice

Cherukuri et al. pin the deuteron magnetic polarizability to 1.3% arXiv:2609.04615, with the two expansion schemes converging from 12% disagreement at NLO to 0.17% at NNLO — the same pionless-EFT/on-shell program that produced Tait’s BBN rate. Allwicher et al. lay out 10⁻⁴-level kaon/pion leptonic ratios as a lepton-universality probe now that lattice matches arXiv:2609.05231, and Romero-López et al. derive the finite-volume formalism to reach the Wess-Zumino-Witten term on the lattice via KK̅→3π arXiv:2609.05006.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.04376 — CMS’s >5σ first observation of spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetry in coherent J/ψ photoproduction; photon polarization inherited by the meson.
  • arXiv:2609.04673 — Dent et al. reframe the LZ event as exothermic DM, dodging the halo-tail bounds that sank the endothermic higgsino.
  • arXiv:2609.04761 — Wang’s LLP flavor tomography fixes the neutrino mass ordering from displaced-lepton ratios alone, free of δ_CP.
  • arXiv:2609.04615 — Deuteron magnetic polarizability to 1.3%; scheme convergence as its own convergence diagnostic.
  • arXiv:2609.04402 — CMS H→Zγ at 200 fb⁻¹, SM-consistent at 1.9σ.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.04868 Higgs Boson Pair Production via Gluon Fusion — Ajjath A H et al. (hep-ph) — updated state-of-the-art gg→hh cross section and uncertainties; the self-coupling thread’s reference number.
  • arXiv:2609.04695 A Differentiable Neural Surrogate for Photon Propagation in Neutrino Telescopes — Yu et al. (astro-ph.HE) — candela, a SIREN photon Green’s function for IceCube, 50–100× faster with end-to-end gradients; the autodiff wave reaching photon transport again.
  • arXiv:2609.04367 Quantum Graph Neural Networks for Jet Tagging on Quantum Hardware — Jobilal et al. (hep-ph) — permutation-invariant QGNN run on IBM/IonQ QPUs, including a first quantum up-vs-down flavor tag.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.04376 — Spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetry of coherent J/ψ photoproduction in hadronic PbPb collisions (CMS Collaboration)

What they did: CMS measured the azimuthal distribution of decay muons from coherently photoproduced J/ψ (reconstructed at p_T<0.2 GeV, 1.6<|y|<2.4) relative to the second-order event plane Ψ_2 in 50–80% central PbPb collisions at 5.36 TeV, using 1.26 nb⁻¹. The cos(2Δϕ) modulation amplitude is A_2=-0.194±0.022 (stat)±0.018 (syst) — negative, and different from zero by more than 5σ, the first such observation for spin-1/2 muons. A_2 shows no significant dependence on rapidity or centrality (7–18% dominant systematic from signal extraction; 3–9% hadronic/incoherent contamination subtracted via a high-p_T fit extrapolation).

Why it matters: Combined with the positive modulation previously seen for spin-0 pions from ρ⁰ decays, this establishes spin-state dependence of azimuthal asymmetries in coherently photoproduced vector-meson decays — direct confirmation that the J/ψ inherits the incident photon’s linear polarization. Crucially, using Ψ_2 rather than the meson-p_T interference proxy makes the polarization handle work across broad rapidity and different collision systems, opening a novel reaction-plane estimator that is less sensitive to nonflow and fluctuations, potentially valuable for small systems like pA. Caveat: the Wu et al. model describes the data well, but the saturation-based Shao et al. calculation overshoots the amplitude by roughly a factor of two, so the theory picture is not settled.

arXiv:2609.04673 — Exothermic and Endothermic Inelastic Dark Matter Interpretations at LZ (James B. Dent et al.)

What they did: Dent and Newstead reinterpret LZ’s single ~248 keV nuclear-recoil event (LZ230616, background 0.0106±0.0008) as exothermic inelastic DM, where the ambient heavier state χ^* down-scatters and dumps its splitting |δ| as recoil, producing a peak at E_0=μ_χN|δ|/m_N. An unbinned shape likelihood fixes the peak to the event energy with σ_p f_≃(0.5–3)×10⁻⁴⁵ cm². The empty high-energy sideband (350–680 keV, zero events) disfavors broad heavy-mass peaks — expected sideband yields per observed event are 0.02 (10 GeV), 19 (42 GeV), 73 (100 GeV) — bounding m_χ≲90 GeV at 95% CL. Excited-state stability then splits solutions into a ~40–90 GeV state with sub-MeV splitting and dark-photon mediator, or a sub-40 GeV state with ~1–10 MeV splitting requiring a leptophobic mediator (to close χ^→χe⁺e⁻).

Why it matters: Exothermic scattering peaks above the elastic endpoint and is largely halo-tail-independent, sidestepping precisely the high-velocity-tail fragility that undermined the endothermic higgsino readings last week. It predicts ≃4.5 events in LZ’s projected 1000-day (~13 tonne-yr) run, and existing XENONnT/PandaX-4T exposures (1.1 and 0.5 expected events) could already test it in extended windows; the μ_χN/m_N peak scaling gives a distinct argon/germanium signature. Caveat: the sideband recast relies on unpublished efficiency/energy-scale extrapolations beyond calibration, and the Helm form factor gives an 𝒪(10⁻⁴⁾ suppression with large uncertainty at this q — the authors stress this is no substitute for a collaboration analysis.

arXiv:2609.04761 — Flavor Tomography of Long-Lived Neutrino-Mass Mediators (Renjie Wang)

What they did: Wang shows that if the long-lived charged particle producing displaced-lepton signals at the HL-LHC is also the mediator generating Majorana neutrino masses (the “shared-coupling condition”), the Casas–Ibarra parametrization fixes the displaced-lepton flavor ratio N_e/N_μ=∑_i|U_ei|² m_i/∑_i|U_μi|² m_i entirely in terms of PMNS data. At NuFit 6.1 best-fit with m_lightest=0: N_e/N_μ=0.140 (normal) vs 2.11 (inverted), a discrimination ratio ℛ=15.1. The prediction holds identically across Scotogenic, Type-III seesaw, inverse/linear seesaw, and lepton-portal DM models (given quasi-degenerate mediators and near-real R). Detector efficiencies cancel in the ratio; δ_CP dependence is <3%. An exact Poisson test gives 3σ ordering discrimination with 𝒪(25) timing-tagged (Δt>200 ps) displaced leptons; Scotogenic yields for M_LLP=300–600 GeV are N_disp≈64–2856.

Why it matters: This is a δ_CP-free collider handle on the mass ordering, structurally immune to the degeneracy that limits T2K/NOvA and complementary to JUNO — because the observable depends on |U_αi|², not U_αi. It sharpens exactly where prior two-HNL flavor-counting proposals (capped at ≲90% classification) are broad. It extends the week’s detector-repurposing theme, exploiting the CMS MTD / ATLAS HGTD timing layers already under construction. Caveats: requires the shared-coupling class (real R, degenerate mediators); complex-R and non-degenerate corrections reach 𝒪(10–30%); the worst-case 3σ scan gives ℛ=8.85, dropping to ℛ≥2.2 for larger m_lightest within the Planck-allowed range; and it presupposes a positive LLP discovery plus Majorana neutrinos.

item.title: Friday, September 4, 2026
item.description:
The higgsino window keeps narrowing

The LZ event is still the center of gravity, but the traffic has shifted from model-building to model-killing. A week after the interpretation glut converged on a ~1.1 TeV endothermic higgsino, the constraints keep arriving: yesterday Pospelov’s solar-capture bound demanded δ>566 keV, and today Rodd et al. arXiv:2609.04175 point out that a thermal higgsino with the required splitting should have deposited events in LZ’s high-energy sideband — which is empty. McCabe arXiv:2609.04181 adds a different discriminant: the same kinematics force the signal into the halo’s high-speed tail, predicting annual modulation above 50%, sometimes 100%. Away from xenon, the day’s real substance sits in a pair of lattice results — a second direct calculation of the θ-induced pion-nucleon coupling, and the first two-hadron form factor from QCD.

Themes

The LZ event, squeezed from both sides

The interpretation stream hasn’t dried up — Chattopadhyay et al. arXiv:2609.02994 fit a sub-TeV singlino, Du et al. arXiv:2609.04163 push the higgsino to intermediate-scale gauginos with a non-universal GUT boundary condition, Smirnov et al. arXiv:2609.04144 give a clean universal treatment across coupled EW multiplets, and Jeesun et al. arXiv:2609.04185 and Unwin arXiv:2609.04186 offer escape routes (atmospheric-ν up-scattering, elastic axion-portal) that dodge the halo-tail dependence entirely. But the useful papers are the ones adding pressure: Rodd’s sideband and McCabe’s modulation both give the collaboration concrete things to check, and both point the same way as yesterday’s solar bound — the higgsino reading is getting hard to sustain.

Strong CP on the lattice, a second determination

He et al. arXiv:2609.04129 compute the CP-violating pion-nucleon coupling g̅_0 from the θ-term on 2+1+1 HISQ ensembles, wrestling with Nπ excited-state contamination and landing at g̅_0/(2F_π)=17.4(1.9)×10⁻³ Θ̅ via the axial Ward identity. This is a direct sibling to Li et al.’s g̃_πNN from late August — the same hadronic-coupling rung above the nEDM, now from a second group and method. The strong-CP thread the memory has tracked since the nEDM/lattice pair is still producing.

Lattice firsts and real-time gauge theory

Ortega-Gama et al. arXiv:2609.04142 report the first QCD determination of an energy-dependent form factor for a two-hadron scattering state (π⁺π⁺ + γ), validating the finite-volume approach against the Ward-Takahashi identity — a genuine methodological milestone toward electroweak responses of resonances. Alongside, two tensor-network papers simulate real-time string breaking in 3+1D U(1) arXiv:2609.04114 and thermalization in open non-Abelian LGT arXiv:2609.04117, extending the quantum-simulation-for-QCD strand toward physical dimensionality.

QCD structure and precision

A spread of structure work: CLAS12’s first near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction on the neutron arXiv:2609.03579, hinting at medium modification of gluon structure; leading-neutron electroproduction for pion PDFs at HERA/EIC arXiv:2609.03368; a CGC Monte Carlo generator, CGC-py arXiv:2609.03434; and a Bayesian pixel-based TMD reconstruction arXiv:2609.03646.

Worth a look

  • arXiv:2609.04175 — Rodd et al.: the empty high-energy sideband as a new handle on the higgsino interpretation, complementing yesterday’s solar bound.
  • arXiv:2609.04181 — McCabe: strong seasonal modulation as a sharp, testable signature of the endothermic reading; XLZD/PandaX can settle it.
  • arXiv:2609.04144 — Smirnov et al.: a universal inelastic-recoil framework across EW multiplets, with a correlated loop-induced elastic prediction.
  • arXiv:2609.04129 — He et al.: second direct lattice g̅_0 from the θ-term; the strong-CP hadronic coupling from a new group.
  • arXiv:2609.04142 — Ortega-Gama et al.: first two-hadron form factor from QCD, a real advance in finite-volume methods.

From the community

A task force on α_s from event shapes arXiv:2609.03002 A Task Force on Strong Coupling Determinations from Event Shapes — Badea et al. (hep-ph) reports its first CERN meeting, aiming to reconcile the persistent spread in event-shape α_s extractions ahead of FCC. And Han et al. arXiv:2609.02950 post a short comment flagging an omission in XENONnT’s recent keV-scale solar-neutrino summary plot — the critique arriving days after the measurement.

Also noted

  • arXiv:2609.02973 Branching fraction measurements of η and η′(958) anomalous decays — LHCb (hep-ex) — most precise B(η→μμ) and first η′(958) search.
  • arXiv:2509.07982 LHAASO Galactic Plane γ-rays Strongly Constrain Heavy Dark Matter — Boehm et al. (hep-ph) — strongest bounds to date on 10⁵–10¹¹ GeV decaying/annihilating DM.
  • arXiv:2609.03879 Multi-tesla operation of high-temperature superconducting cavities — Ahn et al. (hep-ex) — REBCO haloscope cavity, Q₀=1.4×10⁷ at 8 T, ~8× scan-rate gain over copper.

Deep dives

arXiv:2609.04175 — Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with the High-Energy Sideband (Nicholas L. Rodd et al.)

Abstract only. The empty region above the 248 keV event is the discriminant. A thermal 1.1 TeV higgsino tuned to the observed rate and spectrum — splitting δ ~ 370–490 keV depending on the halo model — would, Rodd et al. argue, generically populate a higher-energy sideband along LZ’s S1c axis with additional recoils. LZ reports zero events there, so the higgsino reading sits in mild tension with its own data. The caveat is explicit: the acceptance in that bin is not public, so the tension cannot be quantified without the collaboration’s input — precisely what the authors ask for. They note a non-thermal ~500 GeV higgsino can evade the sideband, and that heavier-target experiments could test the interpretation either way. This is the sideband complement to yesterday’s solar-capture bound: another empty region pushing the same direction, giving LZ a concrete internal cross-check rather than an external astrophysical one.

arXiv:2609.04181 — Seasonal dark matter from the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy event (Christopher McCabe)

The high recoil energy forces the inelastic splitting against the kinematic ceiling set by the halo escape speed, and McCabe turns that into a sharp seasonal signature. A shape-only profile likelihood in the (m_χ, δ) plane confines δ to ~370–400 keV at 1σ for m_χ = 1 TeV, with small splittings disfavored because they place the spectrum below 248 keV. At δ = 350 keV the required v_min = 766 km/s sits just 44 km/s below the maximum lab-frame speed (810 km/s), so the entire signal comes from a thin sliver of the halo tail. The consequence: annual modulation amplitude A = 94% at (1 TeV, 350 keV), rising to 100% at 500 GeV — the rate literally vanishes for up to two-thirds of the year. The modulation is nearly pure timing information (97.2% of discriminating power is arrival-time, not energy correlation) and carries mass information even where spectra are degenerate. Reach: 11 events give 3σ on modulation, 31 give 5σ; XLZD at 200 t·yr reaches 7.5σ, and LZ’s own ~15 t·yr already hits 3σ for δ > 374 keV. A secondary handle is isotopic — ¹³⁶Xe supplies 47% of the rate at δ = 380 keV versus 8.9% natural abundance — though enrichment at scale is unrealistic. Honest caveat, stated twice: everything rests on the Standard Halo Model, precisely in the tail region where it is least trustworthy.

arXiv:2609.04144 — Inelastic Signatures of Electroweak Dark Matter (Juri Smirnov et al.)

Smirnov, Griffith, and Beacom show that Higgs-coupled minimal dark matter — a Majorana plus adjacent Dirac multiplet at the custodial point — reproduces the LZ event through a mechanism that is universal across the whole 3_M2_D through 13_M12_D sequence. The neutral Higgs Clebsch is exactly 1/√2 independent of representation, so both the pseudo-Dirac splitting δ ≃ y²v²/4m_χ and the off-diagonal Z coupling (σ_n^inel ≃ 1.9×10⁻³⁹ cm²) are fixed by (m_χ, y) alone. Requiring one expected inelastic event in LZ’s 2.84 t·yr defines a rate-selected δ_LZ(m_χ) ~ 350–380 keV and a universal band in (m_χ, y); intersecting it with each multiplet’s thermal relic trajectory selects a benchmark, from 3_M2_D at 1.44 TeV to 13_M12_D at 131 TeV. The payoff is a correlated, representation-dependent loop-induced elastic signal — from 1.3×10⁻⁴⁷ cm² up to 5×10⁻⁴⁵ cm² — that must lie above the neutrino floor. Existing null elastic results already disfavor 11_M10_D and 13_M12_D, leaving 3_M2_D, 5_M4_D, 7_M6_D as the preferred survivors, all testable by next-generation searches. Caveats are candidly flagged: the rate estimate uses no full detector-response/likelihood reconstruction; the relic calculation is done in the unbroken phase while the signal depends on sub-MeV broken-phase splittings (argued negligible but unchecked); and it remains a single-event excess. The distinctive value is predictivity — inelastic rate, splitting, and elastic channel are locked together rather than fit independently.

Citation radar

This week’s radar is dominated by a single new experimental anomaly and the theory rush to claim it. Both featured papers, posted the same day (September 1, 2026), interpret the LZ Collaboration’s ~248 keV high-energy nuclear-recoil “event of interest” as inelastic Higgsino dark matter — and both drew ~10 citations almost immediately. Attention is flowing hard toward the oldest, most canonical WIMP candidate suddenly being handed a possible signal, and toward the fact that the TeV Higgsino’s interaction strength is fixed rather than fitted, making it uniquely predictive against the new data.

arXiv:2609.01583 — Higgsino Dark Matter Interpretation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Nuclear-Recoil Event (Katherine Freese et al.)

Freese and Theodosopoulos make the minimal, sharp argument: a nearly pure ~1 TeV Higgsino realizes inelastic dark matter through the off-diagonal Z coupling of two nearly degenerate neutral Majorana states split by δ, and this fixes the inelastic Higgsino–nucleon cross section at σ ≃ 1.86×10⁻³⁹ cm², rather than leaving it free. Using the LZ scalar-to-vector conversion (σ_V ≃ 3.2 σ_SI for xenon), they show the fixed Higgsino prediction falls inside LZ’s two-sided 90% interval for δ ~ 350 keV at m = 1 TeV. Honestly, the paper also concedes tension: rescaling to the thermally preferred 1.1 TeV (via an efficiency-weighted rate ratio ≈0.8) pushes the interval below the prediction, though δ slightly above 350 keV — near xenon’s kinematic ceiling — would recover consistency.

The ~10 citations in days reflect first-mover advantage on a fresh anomaly plus the authors’ prominence. The headline draw is the “no free parameter” framing: the LZ event lands where the most economical SUSY WIMP predicts. The caveats are stated plainly — the rescaling is not a proper LZ likelihood reanalysis — but the provocative claim (a classic candidate matching a real excess) is what the community is picking up.

arXiv:2609.01590 — TeV Higgsino Dark Matter from LZ Nuclear Recoil to Fermi-LAT Gamma Rays (Lei Wu et al.)

Wu, Zhang, and Zhu pursue the same inelastic-Higgsino idea far more ambitiously, welding together three signals under one MSSM benchmark. Freeze-out fixes m ≈ 1.09 TeV; a joint likelihood combining relic density, an energy-only LZ recast, and the 14-year Fermi-LAT Galactic-center excess selects δ ≈ 324 keV. They further argue that destructive interference between tree-level Higgs-exchange and electroweak-loop elastic amplitudes can suppress solar capture/thermalization, evading the 10-year IceCube bound, and that the predicted γγ/γZ line plus endpoint sits near current H.E.S.S. sensitivity and within CTAO’s projected reach. The extensive Supplemental Material builds an internally consistent Einasto–Eddington halo, an annulus-by-annulus Fermi-LAT reweighting, and a response-matched CTAO projection.

The ~10 citations track the same anomaly-driven surge, but this paper’s appeal is different: it packages the LZ interpretation into a fully testable multi-messenger program with near-term falsifiability at CTAO. The authors are unusually candid that their LZ proxy is not the official likelihood and that the IceCube cancellation band is only shown to be “parametrically possible,” not located. Its citations likely accrue as the more complete reference framework for anyone extending the Higgsino-LZ story to indirect detection.
